title: Advisory Regarding Luxury Goods and Wholesale Club Transaction Risks with Iranian Officials Under the Foreign Missions Act
text: hide Advisory Regarding Luxury Goods and Wholesale Club Transaction Risks with Iranian Officials Under the Foreign Missions Act Other Release Bureau of Arms Control and Nonproliferation September 22, 2026 The United States Department of State is issuing this advisory to alert wholesale club stores and luxury goods retailers and related industries in the New York metropolitan area to legal restrictions associated with Iranian officials’ access to wholesale club stores and luxury goods. In addition, there are potential sanctions compliance risks under U.S. and United Nations (UN) sanctions authorities. These risks are heightened on the margins of the opening of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), which typically occurs in September each year. [1] Following the Department of State’s September 18, 2025, determination pursuant to the Foreign Missions Act, the Permanent Mission of the Islamic Republic of Iran to the UN and its members, including Iranian government officials traveling for UN purposes, and their dependents, are required to obtain approval from the Department of State prior to acquiring membership in or items from any wholesale club store in the United States or luxury goods in the United States. [2] The United States will not allow the Iranian regime to exploit diplomatic activities, including travel to the UN, to further enrich Iranian officials. The regime’s officials responsible for diverting funds from the Iranian population towards its destabilizing proliferation-sensitive programs must not be allowed to obtain goods unavailable to the Iranian public. The United States will continue to take vigilant action to hold the regime accountable and uphold U.S. and UN restrictive measures and sanctions and urges all businesses to exercise heightened due diligence. Legal Restrictions As outlined in Department of State’s September 18, 2025, determination pursuant to section 204(b) of the Foreign Missions Act, the Permanent Mission of the Islamic Republic of Iran to the United Nations and its members, including Iranian government officials traveling for UN purposes, and their dependents, are required to obtain approval from the Department of State prior to acquiring access to any wholesale club store or its merchandise or acquiring luxury goods through any means in the United States. [3] Luxury retailers and wholesale club stores should be aware of this requirement when transacting with the Permanent Mission of the Islamic Republic of Iran to the United Nations and its members, including Iranian government officials traveling for UN purposes, and their dependents. Such Iranian delegation members are restricted in their travel within the New York metropolitan area. [4] As a result, luxury retailers and service providers in New York, New Jersey, and Connecticut should exercise heightened caution. Moreover, additional Iranian officials and their dependents not permanently assigned to the Permanent Mission of the Islamic Republic of Iran typically are accredited to attend the opening of the UNGA, which usually occurs in September each year. As a result, wholesale club stores and luxury goods retailers should be especially attentive of the heightened compliance risks during such times. Luxury goods are defined under Foreign Missions Act Designation No. 2025-06 as any of the following items that, unless otherwise specified, are valued over $1,000, before tax, per item: watches (including wristwatches, pocket-watches, and other watches); leather apparel and clothing accessories; silk apparel and clothing accessories; footwear; fur skins and artificial furs; handbags; wallets; fountain pens; cosmetics; perfumes and toilet waters; works of art (including paintings, original sculptures, and statuary); antiques (more than 100 years old); carpets, rugs, or tapestries; pearls, gems, and precious and semi-precious stones; jewelry with pearls, gems, or precious or semi-precious stones; jewelry of precious metal or of metal clad with precious metal; electronic items and appliances; recreational sports articles and equipment; musical instruments; cigarettes and cigars; wine, spirits, beer, and spirituous beverages; and personal automobiles and other personal motor vehicles valued over $60,000, before tax. [5] Department of State approval is also required for the acquisition of membership in wholesale club stores and acquisition by any means of any items from wholesale club stores. Iran-Related Sanctions In addition to the specific risks of transacting with Iranian officials in relation to wholesale club stores and items and luxury goods, the United States maintains several sanctions programs related to Iran that could have implications for officials seeking to conduct transactions in the United States. Iran operates sophisticated procurement networks designed to circumvent export controls and acquire dual-use goods and technologies in furtherance of its nuclear and ballistic missile programs. Furthermore, the purchase of luxury goods by Iranian officials may constitute a form of sanctions evasion and proliferation financing, as such goods can be monetized or bartered to support illicit procurement activities. U.S. persons, including businesses operating in the United States, are generally prohibited from engaging in transactions with individuals or entities on the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (“SDN List”) maintained by the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), regardless of the purpose or location of the transaction. Iran-related sanctions fall under several programs, including but not limited to: The Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations, 31 C.F.R. part 560 (ITSR); Executive Order (E.O.) 13224, as amended (counterterrorism); E.O. 13382 (weapons of mass destruction proliferation); E.O. 13876 (Iranian government officials); and E.O. 13949 (Iranian conventional arms proliferation). For the most accurate list of U.S. sanctions and other restrictive measures on Iranian persons, the United States encourages all entities and individuals to refer to the Sanctions List Search Tool maintained by OFAC and the Consolidated Screening List (CSL) maintained by the Department of Commerce’s International Trade Administration. Furthermore, the Iran-related United Nations Security Council resolutions (UNSCR) 1696 (2006), 1747 (2007), 1803 (2008), 1835 (2008), and 1929 (2010) were reimposed at 8:00 pm Eastern Time on September 27, 2025, based on Iran’s continuing “significant non-performance” of its nuclear commitments. [6] As a result, UN measures previously suspended are now reimposed on Iran, including provisions that reimpose travel bans and global asset freezes on listed persons. The list of Iranian entities and individuals subject to UN sanctions can be found on the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List . With respect to individuals subject to sanctions, businesses must implement and enforce sanctions compliance procedures, including verifying customer identity and beneficial ownership; screening customers against the SDN List before completing high-value transactions; and maintaining records of screening efforts. The U.S. Government expects companies to have effective and comprehensive procedures; companies can implement various practices to ensure robust compliance with their obligations. These practices include training staff on sanctions compliance, establishing clear escalation procedures for suspicious transactions, documenting compliance decisions, and consulting with legal counsel when there is uncertainty. Potential red flags may include: Requests to ship goods to Iran or third countries and requests to obscure the identity of the ultimate recipient; Large cash payments or structured transactions designed to avoid reporting thresholds; Unusual payment arrangements, such as payments from an unrelated third party, multiple unrelated payors, or requests for refunds to an account different from the original payer; Requests to split or modify transactions without a legitimate explanation, particularly where the purpose appears to be aimed at avoiding compliance review or reporting requirements; Attempts to exploit diplomatic or foreign mission status as a reason for preferential treatment, exemption from normal business controls, or avoidance of documentation; Customers who are evasive about their identity or purpose, or requests involving diplomats, foreign government officials, or purported “government representatives” where the customer’s affiliation, or purpose cannot readily be verified; Unexplained changes in the customer, purchaser, consignee, or end-user after an order is placed; Requests to misdescribe goods on purchase invoices or customs documents; Pressure to bypass compliance procedures, such as requests to skip customer identification or export classification; Transactions that do not make commercial sense, such as circuitous shipping routes or pricing inconsistent with the transaction, or the use of shell companies or intermediaries for personal purchases; Use of personal accounts/addresses for commercial transactions and vice versa; Evasiveness when asked routine compliance questions, especially when the customer changes its explanation, refuses to provide supporting documents, or insists that the business not ask questions; and A mismatch between the customer’s nationality or location and its actual operational footprint, including unexplained use of Iranian phone numbers, email addresses, or physical addresses. No single red flag is necessarily determinative. Businesses should consider the totality of the circumstances and escalate transactions accordingly, using the screening lists and resources provided in this Advisory. Enforcement Actions and Penalties Pursuant to section 211 of the Foreign Missions Act, it shall be unlawful for any person to make available any benefits to a foreign mission contrary to the requirements set forth in the Department of State’s September 18, 2025, determination. Additionally, private industry should be aware of the potential consequences for engaging in or facilitating prohibited or sanctionable conduct. OFAC investigates apparent violations of its regulations and maintains enforcement authority as outlined in its Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines, 31 C.F.R. Part 501, Appendix A. Persons who violate U.S. sanctions with respect to Iran can be subject to civil monetary penalties equal to the greater of $377,700 per violation or twice the value of the transaction, referred for criminal prosecution, or both. For additional information regarding OFAC’s enforcement authorities, Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines, and recent civil penalties and enforcement actions, visit the OFAC Resource Center. Additional Information and Resources For questions regarding designations and determinations made under the Foreign Missions Act, contact the Department of State’s Office of Foreign Missions at the following email address: OFM-Policy@state.gov . Businesses that identify potential sanctions violations should consult legal counsel and consider voluntary self-disclosures to OFAC. Violations can be reported to OFAC at the following email address: OFACDisclosures@treasury.gov . For questions regarding compliance matters, please contact the OFAC Compliance Hotline . For questions regarding this advisory, contact the Department of State’s Bureau of Arms Control and Nonproliferation at the following email address: ACN_sanctions@state.gov . The Department of State urges all businesses in the wholesale club stores and luxury goods sectors to review and strengthen their sanctions compliance programs ahead of UNGA in September 2026. Proactive compliance measures protect both your businesses and U.S. national security interests. This advisory is limited to considerations that may arise under U.S. legal authorities. Businesses operating in multiple jurisdictions should familiarize themselves with applicable third-country laws and regulations. ↑ Department of State Public Notice #12834 “Designation Pursuant to the Foreign Missions Act,” September 23, 2025 . ↑ Department of State Public Notice #12834 “Designation Pursuant to the Foreign Missions Act,” September 23, 2025 . ↑ Restrictions on the Iranian United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) Delegation’s Movement and Acquiring Items from Wholesale Club Stores and Luxury Goods, September 22, 2025 . ↑ Department of State Public Notice #12834 “Designation Pursuant to the Foreign Missions Act,” September 23, 2025 . ↑ Completion of UN Sanctions Snapback on Iran, September 27, 2025 . ↑ Tags Bureau of Arms Control and Nonproliferation Bureau of Near Eastern Affairs Iran Office of Foreign Missions Sanctions and Designations UNGA81 United Nations General Assembly (UNGA)

title: Ukraine – Air Defense Development Upgrade
text: hide Ukraine – Air Defense Development Upgrade Foreign Military Sales: Congressional Notification Bureau of Political-Military Affairs September 18, 2026 Transmittal #26-90 The U.S. Department of State has made a determination approving a possible Foreign Military Sale to the Government of Ukraine for purchase of Air Defense Development Upgrades and related equipment and services. The estimated total cost is $2.68 billion. If the proposed purchase is concluded, Ukraine would finance it using a combination of European contributions and U.S. Foreign Military Financing appropriated during the prior Administration. The FMF will be counted as a U.S. capital contribution to the Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund via a 1:1 reimbursement. The Government of Ukraine has requested to buy the following non-major defense equipment items: S-300 Clone missiles; GAM-67 missiles; Range-Extended Air Defense Laser Guided Rocket missile systems; Improvised Transporter Erector Launcher 1.5; mobile launching system modification kits; RPS 202 counter-Unmanned Aircraft System radars; erectable mast trailers, major modifications, and maintenance support; spare parts, consumables and accessories, and repair and return support; software; publications; transportation support; U.S. Government and contractor engineering, technical, and logistics support services; and other related elements of logistics and program support. This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a partner country that is a force for political and economic progress in Europe. The proposed sale will improve Ukraine’s capability to meet current and future threats by further equipping it to conduct self-defense and regional security missions with a more robust air defense capability. Ukraine will have no difficulty absorbing these articles and services into its armed forces. The proposed sale of this equipment and support will not alter the basic military balance in the region. The principal contractor(s) will be selected through competitive procurements conducted by the U.S. Government in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation. At this time, the U.S. Government is not aware of any offset agreement proposed in connection with this potential sale. Any offset agreement will be defined in negotiations between the purchaser and the contractor(s). Implementation of this proposed sale will not require the assignment of any additional U.S. Government or contractor representatives to Ukraine. There will be no adverse impact on U.S. defense readiness as a result of this proposed sale. For further information, please contact the Bureau of Political-Military Affairs Outreach Team at T_Outreach_PM@State.gov . title: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia – F-35 Lightning II Joint Strike Fighter Aircraft
text: hide Kingdom of Saudi Arabia – F-35 Lightning II Joint Strike Fighter Aircraft Foreign Military Sales: Congressional Notification Bureau of Political-Military Affairs September 17, 2026 Transmittal #26-69 The U.S. Department of State has made a determination approving a possible foreign military sale to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for their purchase of F-35 Lightning II Joint Strike Fighter and related equipment. The estimated total cost is $24.3 billion. The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia has requested to buy forty-eight (48) F-35 Lightning II Joint Strike Fighter aircraft with conventional takeoff and landing; and forty-nine (49) Pratt & Whitney F135-PW-100 engines (48 installed, 1 spare). The following non-MDE items will also be included: AN/PYQ-10 simple key loaders; KIV-78 cryptographic appliques; secure communications, precision navigation, and cryptographic devices; electronic warfare database support; cartridge actuated devices/propellant actuated devices; aircraft and munitions support and support equipment; spare parts, consumables and accessories, and repair and return support; training aids, devices, and spare parts; engine component improvement program; major and minor modifications and maintenance support; classified and unclassified software delivery and support; classified and unclassified publications and technical documentation; transportation, ferry, and refueling support; personnel training and training equipment, including simulators; clothing, textiles, and individual equipment; studies and surveys; site surveys; U.S. Government and engineering, technical, and logistics support services; and other related elements of logistics and program support. This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a major non-NATO ally that is a force for political stability and economic progress in the Gulf region. The proposed sale will improve Saudi Arabia’s capability to deter current and future threats by strengthening its homeland defense, and improving interoperability with U.S. forces, and other regional and NATO forces. The proposed sale will also augment Saudi Arabia’s operational aircraft and enhance its air-to-air, and air-to-ground self-defense capability. The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia will have no difficulty absorbing this equipment and services into its armed forces. The proposed sale of this equipment and support will not alter the military balance in the region. The principal contractors will be Lockheed Martin Aeronautics Company, located in Fort Worth, Texas; and Pratt & Whitney Military Engines, located in East Hartford, Connecticut. At this time, the U.S. Government is not aware of any offset agreement proposed in connection with this potential sale. Any offset agreement will be defined in negotiations between the purchaser and contractor. Implementation of this proposed sale will not require the assignment of any additional U.S. Government or contractor representatives to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. There will be no adverse impact on U.S. defense readiness as a result of this proposed sale. For further information, please contact the Bureau of Political-Military Affairs Outreach Team at T_Outreach_PM@State.gov. title: New U.S Health Partnership with Vietnam Under the Trump Administration’s America First Global Health Strategy
text: hide New U.S Health Partnership with Vietnam Under the Trump Administration’s America First Global Health Strategy Press Statement Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesman Office of the Spokesman September 14, 2026 On September 11, the United States and Vietnam signed a five-year bilateral Health Cooperation Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) under the Trump Administration’s America First Global Health Strategy (AFGHS), advancing our new model of co-investment in global health. Through this MOU, the Department of State, working with Congress, plans to provide $98,750,000 in life-saving global health assistance over the next five years, including $21,385,000 in dedicated Global Health Security funding, to support Vietnam’s transition to full country ownership of its HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis programs while strengthening its capacity to detect and respond to emerging and re-emerging infectious disease threats. Vietnam is well-positioned to assume this responsibility and concurrent to this MOU, their annual health expenditure is projected to grow by approximately $10.5 billion over the five-year MOU period, from $23.3 billion to $33.8 billion. This five-year partnership ensures that the gains achieved through more than two decades of U.S. support are preserved, owned, and sustained by Vietnam’s own health institutions. As Vietnam charts a new path for its health care system, this partnership is expected to deliver measurable results over the next five years. HIV and TB programming will fully transition to Vietnamese ownership within that period. Vietnam will move closer to its HIV epidemic-control targets through expanded prevention, case finding, and treatment, backed by greater domestic ownership and sustainability. Earlier detection and treatment of tuberculosis will reduce transmission, morbidity, and mortality, while lowering the risk of drug-resistant TB reaching the United States. This new five-year phase of U.S.–Vietnam health cooperation builds on the strong foundation of our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, complementing our robust ties in trade, security, and innovation. The America First Global Health Strategy reflects the Trump Administration’s commitment to protecting Americans from infectious disease threats, ending cycles of dependency, and building durable, country-led health systems around the world. America First Global Health Strategy Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) signed so far represent more than $24.7 billion in new health funding, including more than $14.6 billion in U.S. assistance alongside more than $10.1 billion in co-investment from recipient countries, building on decades of progress fighting HIV/AIDS, malaria, tuberculosis, and other infectious diseases around the world. As of September 11, the State Department has signed 35 bilateral global health MOUs with Angola, Bolivia, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cambodia, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Guatemala, Guinea, Honduras, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mozambique, Niger, Nigeria, Panama, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Rwanda, Senegal, Sierra Leone, South Sudan, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Uganda, and Vietnam. title: U.S. Department of State Concludes $36 Million Settlement Resolving Export Violations by BAE Systems, Inc. (BAE)
text: hide U.S. Department of State Concludes $36 Million Settlement Resolving Export Violations by BAE Systems, Inc. (BAE) Media Note Bureau of Political-Military Affairs August 13, 2026 The U.S. Department of State has concluded an administrative settlement with BAE to resolve 104 violations of the Arms Export Control Act (AECA), 22 U.S.C. § 2751 et seq., and the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), 22 C.F.R. parts 120-130. The Department of State and BAE reached this settlement following an extensive compliance review by the Office of Defense Trade Controls Compliance in the Department’s Bureau of Political-Military Affairs. The administrative settlement between the Department of State and BAE, concluded pursuant to ITAR § 128.11, addresses multiple categories of ITAR violations, including BAE’s unauthorized exports of technical data to multiple countries, including in one instance to China; violations of terms, conditions, and provisos of several Directorate of Defense Trade Controls authorizations involving various countries; and unauthorized exports of defense articles, including technical data, designated as Significant Military Equipment. BAE voluntarily disclosed all but one of the alleged violations, a substantial portion of which predate 2023. BAE also fully cooperated with the Department’s review of this matter and has implemented numerous improvements to its ITAR compliance program since the conduct at issue. Under the terms of the 36-month consent agreement, BAE will pay a civil penalty of $36 million. The Department has agreed to suspend $18 million of this amount on the condition that the funds will be used for the Department-approved Consent Agreement’s remedial compliance measures to strengthen BAE’s compliance program. In addition, for an initial period of at least 24 months, BAE will engage an external Special Compliance Officer to oversee the consent agreement, which will also require at least one external audit of its ITAR compliance program and implementation of additional compliance measures. This settlement demonstrates the Department’s role in furthering the national security and foreign policy of the United States by controlling the export of defense articles. The settlement also highlights the importance of exporting defense articles pursuant only to appropriate authorization from the Department. The Consent Agreement and related documents will be available for public inspection in the Public Reading Room of the Department of State and on the Penalties and Oversights Agreements section of the DDTC’s website. For additional information, please contact the Office of the Under Secretary for Arms Control and International Security at T_Outreach_PM@state.gov . title: Dismantling Transnational Criminal Organization Xinbi Guarantee
text: hide Dismantling Transnational Criminal Organization Xinbi Guarantee Press Statement Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesman Office of the Spokesperson September 9, 2026 As part of President Trump’s mission to combat cybercrime, fraud, and predatory schemes against American citizens, the United States is sanctioning Xinbi Guarantee—a Chinese-language platform used extensively by transnational criminal organizations and money laundering networks behind cyber scam operations targeting Americans—along with two entities that supported Xinbi Guarantee’s core operations. These sanctions are being implemented by the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). Scam centers in Southeast Asia steal billions of dollars from American victims each year. Xinbi Guarantee operates a large illicit online marketplace that is used to support cyber scams, fraud, money laundering, and other criminal activity targeting Americans. The Trump Administration will not let insidious criminal networks prey on the American people—cybercrime, fraud, and predatory schemes end here. Today’s actions were taken in furtherance of Executive Order (E.O.) 14390 “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens” and pursuant to E.O. 13581 “Blocking Property of Transnational Criminal Organizations,” as amended by E.O. 13863. title: Strengthening U.S. Ties with the Pacific: Deputy Secretary Landau Engages Partners in Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Kiribati
text: hide Strengthening U.S. Ties with the Pacific: Deputy Secretary Landau Engages Partners in Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Kiribati Media Note Office of the Spokesperson September 11, 2026 Fresh from his meetings with government partners at the Pacific Islands Forum in Palau, Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau traveled to the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM), Solomon Islands, and Kiribati to advance the Trump Administration’s America First economic and security priorities across the Pacific. The Deputy Secretary reaffirmed our commitment to the FSM in a bilateral meeting with FSM President Wesley Simina. The Deputy Secretary also surveyed the recovery efforts following Typhoon Sinlaku’s damage in Chuuk State where he announced the United States intends to provide over $100 million to support disaster relief and reconstruction in FSM, delivering on U.S. commitments under the Compact of Free Association. In Solomon Islands, the Deputy Secretary emphasized the bonds forged during World War II and outlined a vision for mutual progress in a free and open Pacific. He paid his respects at Guadalcanal, Red Beach, and Bloody Ridge Memorials where Americans, Solomon Islanders, and other Allied forces sacrificed their lives to turn the tide of the war. The Deputy Secretary announced U.S. support through the Ambassadors Fund for Cultural Preservation for the preservation of the Bloody Ridge battlefield as a site of perpetual remembrance and continuing education. Looking forward, he signed an agreement with Minister for Foreign Affairs and External Trade Rick Houenipwela for the Peace Corps to return to the Solomon Islands after a 26-year absence. At Honiara Airport, he concluded his visit by announcing that the U.S. Department of State, working with Congress, intends to provide four aircraft rescue and firefighting vehicles to enhance the safety of American and international tourists. He also announced the Millenium Challenge Corporation will conduct a condition assessment to determine the cost of rehabilitating the Solomon Islands Parliament. In Kiribati, the Deputy Secretary attended the Kiribati Development Partners Forum on Kiritimati Island at the invitation of President Taneti Maamau to emphasize U.S. commitment to partnership with Kiribati on economic development in line with the Kiribati 20-Year Vision. The Deputy Secretary announced the Millenium Challenge Corporation will conduct a study to update and expand the wharf on Kiritimati Island. This initiative will lay the foundation for a long-term infrastructure investment to increase access to trade and support maritime security and combatting illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing for the peoples of Kiritimati. Throughout the visit, the Deputy Secretary reaffirmed the United States’ longstanding commitment to partnering with Pacific Island nations to expand economic and commercial opportunities, strengthen digital connectivity, combat transnational criminal activity, and safeguard global health security. Meeting with senior leaders in each country, he unveiled new initiatives to advance a free and open Pacific, expand opportunities for U.S. businesses, and deliver concrete economic results for the American taxpayer. title: Terrorist Designation of Los Tiguerones
text: hide Terrorist Designation of Los Tiguerones Press Statement Marco Rubio, Secretary of State September 9, 2026 Today, the U.S. Department of State is designating Los Tiguerones as a Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO) and a Specially Designated Global Terrorist. Los Tiguerones is an Ecuador-based gang linked to narcotrafficking and other illicit activity, along with numerous attacks targeting civilians, law enforcement officers, and journalists, including the live takeover of an Ecuadorian television station in 2024. The Trump Administration will continue to use all available tools to protect our nation by keeping illicit drugs off our streets and disrupting the revenue streams funding violent narcoterrorists. Today’s action taken by the State Department further demonstrates that the Trump Administration continues to deliver on its promises to the American people to dismantle cartels and narcoterrorist networks in our region, ensuring the safety of the American people. Terrorist designations expose and isolate entities and individuals, denying them access to the U.S. financial system and the resources they need to carry out attacks. As a result of actions taken today, all property and interests in property of those designated today that are in the United States or that are in possession or control of a U.S. person are blocked, and U.S. persons are generally prohibited from engaging in transactions with them. Moreover, designations can assist law enforcement actions of other U.S. agencies and governments. Today’s actions are taken pursuant to section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act and Executive Order 13224. FTO designations go into effect upon publication in the Federal Register . title: Launch of the Space Catalyst Partnership to Secure American Commercial Space Superiority
text: hide Launch of the Space Catalyst Partnership to Secure American Commercial Space Superiority Fact Sheet Office of the Spokesperson September 10, 2026 The Space Catalyst Partnership (SCP), the Department of State’s flagship initiative to deepen civil and commercial space cooperation between the United States and Artemis Accords signatory countries, was launched today in Lima, Peru. The SCP aims to create opportunities for foreign governments, industry, space agencies, and research organizations to benefit from the vibrant U.S. space ecosystem through commercial partnerships and scientific collaboration, while ensuring outer space is used safely, peacefully, and transparently to the benefit of mankind. As part of the SCP, the Department is working with Congress to launch a $6.5 million rural connectivity project to offer satellite-based internet to rural schools, small businesses, community centers, and public institutions across Peru’s southern regions. This project is among the first SCP projects that, subject to the availability of funds, will assist priority countries’ efforts to integrate space-related technology and services into their economies. The SCP will primarily promote civil and commercial space cooperation through three tools: diplomatic outreach, industry engagement, and the targeted use of foreign assistance, subject to the availability of funds. Potential activities under the SCP include: Diplomatic Outreach Coordinating across U.S. government agencies to help partner countries gain access to American space technology and services, including assistance in securing U.S. government financing for major projects. Expanding the number of space-focused trade delegations to foster deeper collaboration between the United States, key partner countries, and the private sector. Aligning the scientific experiments, equipment, and other capabilities of foreign space agencies and research institutions in support of U.S.-led civil space activities, including through partnerships with American companies. Foreign Assistance Deploying targeted foreign assistance to procure U.S. space goods and services for the benefit of emerging spacefaring countries, starting with the aforementioned $6.5 million Peruvian rural connectivity project. Integrating U.S. space capabilities in public and private organizations to drive economic prosperity and scientific advancement in other sectors, such as critical minerals, agriculture, transportation, communications, finance, energy, and pharmaceuticals. Industry Engagement Connecting American companies with new customers and helping foreign countries to navigate the U.S. commercial space ecosystem to create new partnerships with U.S. companies and learn best practices for fostering the growth of a vibrant space industry. Accelerating direct industry-to-customer engagement opportunities in the Western Hemisphere, East Asia and the Pacific, and other priority markets to help American firms compete effectively and give prospective users direct access to the world-class space technology and services. Leveraging the Department’s diplomatic platforms to promote American industry at international commercial space trade shows, forums, and events, including in emerging space markets. Strengthening relationships with American space companies, through industry briefings and roundtables, to ensure U.S. industry priorities inform the Department’s diplomatic engagements. For media inquiries, please submit a request . For further information for partner countries and companies, please contact SpaceCatalyst@state.gov. title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Ecuadorian Foreign Minister Roberto Kury Deliver Statements
text: hide Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Ecuadorian Foreign Minister Roberto Kury Deliver Statements Remarks Marco Rubio, Secretary of State Roberto Kury Pesantes, Ecuadorian Foreign Minister of Human Mobility Palacio de Carondelet Quito, Ecuador September 10, 2026 MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) We are receiving Secretary of State Marco Rubio from the United States of America, and also Roberto Kury Pesantes, the Foreign Minister of Ecuador. Ladies and gentlemen, dear authorities, representatives from the press that are here with us today, please, everybody be welcome to this joint press release on behalf of Secretary of State Marco Rubio from the United States of America and Roberto Kury Pesantes, Foreign Minister of Ecuador. In this space we will be able to share the main findings of this day. Now we would like to invite Foreign Minister Roberto Kury, Foreign Minister of Human Mobility of Ecuador. FOREIGN MINISTER KURY: (Via interpreter) Good afternoon to all of the representatives of the press that are here with us today. For us it’s an absolute honor to be hosting you and hosting the second official visit on behalf of the Secretary of State of the United States, Marco Rubio. This visit is not only a very important diplomatic milestone, but it also reflects the excellent moment that Ecuador and the United States are undergoing jointly with our administrations; and overall, it is a very clear example that we are sharing a common vision – a vision that is focused on security; that is focused on liberty, on democracy, and overall on shared prosperity. I would like to structure my presentation in three axes, which is something that we constantly work with the United States. One is the issue related to safety – our shared safety and security, focused on fighting against transnational threats, and also the threats that we are confronting right now are not only local; they know no boundaries. And in the same way we do need to tackle them in a way that is multinational and coordinated not only locally. Ecuador has assumed a very firm, brave, and decisive role in the region to try to break down these criminal organizations and drug-dealing bands that try to cause harm to our families and to our peace and to our institutions. Therefore, technical operation and political support are fundamental parts of the puzzle for this effort, and today we want to restate that the institutional strength and the exchange of intelligence, the strengthening of our capabilities, are the only way forward in order to be able to bring back the absolute peace for our peoples. Secondly, I would also like to mention the issue related to economy. Sustainable peace cannot be sustained only through security and safety, but it is also very necessary to have economic development, employment, and real opportunities for our people. Therefore, Ecuador has positioned itself as a strategic partner that is trustworthy, that opens the door for hemispheric trade in different sectors in order to be able to jointly work with the United States of America. And finally, the third axis I would like to sum up: that this is a partnership not only at the diplomatic level, and it’s not a short-term partnership; our relationship with the United States is envisioned to be lasting because our nations go beyond a simple political moment. They share democratic values and the commitment for the well-being of our nations. This visit on behalf of Secretary Rubio allows us to create a pragmatic roadmap, and a very ambitious roadmap, for the upcoming years, ensuring that our political dialogue can be translated into tangible results for each and every one of our citizens and our region. Dear Secretary, your presence here in our Ecuadorian soil really ratifies that not only are we working hand in hand, but also that we are working for a better future for both nations. Be confident that in us you will find a country that is a loyal ally, an active ally, and a decisive ally to be able to build a safer hemisphere, a free hemisphere, and prosperous hemisphere. Thank you very much. MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Thank you very much, dear Foreign Minister. Now we would like to invite the intervention of Marco Rubio, the Secretary of State of the United States of America. SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) Thank you very much for this opportunity to be here with you again. A year and three days ago I came; this is my second official visit as the Secretary of State, and my third visit, because I came as a senator before as well. And we will see ourselves in September for sure once again, or in – even closer than next September. And thank you very much for this opportunity. The partnership between the United States and Ecuador – I’m going to share some words in English as well, just so that people don’t get offended with me, as well for my press, English-speaking press that we have from the United States. But first of all I would like to say that this partnership between – of our countries is very important. We do not have a better ally in the region with regards to confronting the big threat of criminal transnational organizations. It’s criminal transnational organization that has changed over the last few years. We had been used to criminal groups that cooperated within a national boundary, but now we see networks of terrorist organizations. Let’s not call them criminal groups; they’re terrorist groups that are attacking country after country, threatening the state, the well-being, the health, and the safety of our people. And in order to be able to discuss transnational issues we have to create a coalition of countries. And one of the countries that has participated most actively and is doing the most to confront this is Ecuador, and that’s why we’re here with you today. And we’re doing a lot of things together. Our elite forces are working jointly on a day-to-day basis in a way that has no precedence in order to try to dismantle these terrorist organizations which are causing so much harm to this country, to our country, and to plenty of other countries in our region. At the same time, we have worked – and I’m going to ask the United States Congress for 45 additional million dollars – to continue contributing towards this effort of dismantling these terrorist groups and finishing with them once and for all. At the same time, we are launching a $10 million effort in order to be able to tackle illegal mining that is stealing the riches of your country. They should be towards the benefit of people, not towards the benefit of a terrorist group. And we will also start with that initiative. I want to announce that we are giving a fleet from the U.S. Coast Guard here to Ecuador so that they are able to use it. It’s a 110-feet vessel. And on top of that, we will transfer five more interceptor vessels in the upcoming months. We will have a total of 12 total vessels – 12 of them – over the last year. And we also want to say that the results are evident. You have been able to have your interventions and have been able to see a historical numbers of seizures of drugs over the last year, which is something that was previously never before seen. I must say that as part of the effort, the administration of – President Trump’s administration has sanctioned 15 entities – criminal organizations, terrorist organizations, and also two individual people. And we have identified 10 commercial fishing companies, and we – that were also participating in illegal actions. And this is very important; we continue working on this. And today, we have made the decision on behalf of the United States Government to designate Los Tiburones as another terrorist group, and this is on top of the things that we have done with Los Choneros and with Los Lobos and other groups that are not coming up to my mind at this point in time. But yeah, it was the three additional groups, and today with the Tiburones as well. These criminal groups – and I’m going to repeat what I said before because it’s very important for us to highlight this. We’re not talking about mafia, normal mafia. We’re not talking about criminals. We’re talking about terrorists – terrorists that in many cases have weapons and equipment that is very similar to those from armies of certain countries. These are not common groups. They participate in common crime, of course, but they have capabilities beyond that. They’re terrorist groups. And that is something that we have to confront, we have to dismantle, and we have to beat them. And we are fully committed for that. At the same time, we have also worked on economic issues. There’s huge economic opportunities. The number one responsibility of government is the safety of the people in the country, but beyond that we do need to have prosperity, economic opportunities. And there are huge economic opportunities. Your economy is growing. It’s growing at a very impressive level, but it could even take that step further. It could accelerate even further for the benefit of the people. And we are trying to find what opportunities exist, and we know that there’s plenty of them so that United States economy and Ecuadorian economy can participate jointly to create this prosperity, which would help both countries. So with all of this, we are fully committed – 100 percent committed – and I wanted to come here as part of this official visit to add this and to keep on working on all of these things, and to have very concrete achievements like the ones we have obtained over the last year. Because oftentimes, when you come on these visits, we say and we talk about what we will do, but we have already done things, and we will even work harder. And hopefully next time we’re here we will have many more achievements that we can talk about, and also we will still have a lot to do. So thank you very much for that, and I’m going to share a couple of words in English. (In English) Just in English, first of all, I want to thank the foreign minister; I want to thank President Noboa and their administration. They’ve been incredible partners. They’re a key leader in the Shield of the Americas and in the Counter Cartel Coalition, the American – Americas Counter Cartel Coalition. In fact, they are the most involved and aggressive partner we have in that regard. Our – as we speak right now, our elite forces are operating jointly, going after criminal groups, dismantling narco networks, and bringing people to justice that had never been brough to justice before. And I think it’s important to point for a second that the groups we are taking on, these are terrorist organizations. These are not just criminal organizations. These are not just narco organizations. These are terrorist organizations. They have to be confronted, and they have to be dismantled. And that’s what we’re working on together in a way that really has no precedent, and we’re going to be doing more. For example, we’ll be asking Congress for another $45 million of new commitments to help Ecuador, working with us, to take this effort on. We’re going to be asking for $10 million as well, or we’re going to be launching an initiative – $10 million of approved projects to go after illegal gold mining and gang recruitment and illicit finance and land and maritime drug trafficking. I’m pleased to announce today that, as part of this effort, we’ll be delivering a 110-foot U.S. Coast Guard cutter to Ecuador so that that will help strengthen their navy and their ability to stop maritime narcotic trafficking and weapons shipments and illegal fishing, and a range of other threats. And we’re going to do more than just that. Next month, we’ll be transferring five more interceptor vessels. That’ll bring to a total of 12 this year – 12 this year. Again, the progress we’ve made on this relationship really has no historic precedent, and there’s so much more to do. And the results are there. You see it already. I was just told this before we got here today that the Ecuadorian navy has seized 2.5 metric tons of cocaine using these vessels that we were able to provide. They’re doing their part, and we’re going to continue to do ours. By the way, we’ve sanctioned a network of 15 entities and individuals and identified 10 commercial fishing vessels as blocked property. These are things that were being used to facilitate narcotrafficking and other things. Now, today we’ll be designating a new group and another group as a Foreign Terrorist Organization, a group known as Los Tiburones. And this comes on the heels of our designation of three other groups, including Los Lobos and Los Choneros, in July. These are organizations – as I said, they’re not ordinary. These are violent, bloodthirsty terrorist organizations, and we have to make sure that we continue to pursue them. And as we dismantle these terrorist organizations, we also have to go after corrupt officials that collaborate and conspire with these terrorists. We’ll be announcing the designation of seven former members of the government here, officials, for accepting bribes and for betraying their most essential duties on behalf of – and they did this on behalf of these terrorist organizations, these dangerous criminal groups. There was so much more for us to do. We’ve signed a bilateral critical minerals framework earlier this year to collaborate on price challenges and to spur development. We’re going to kick off our Millennium Challenge Corporation Compact with Ecuador. We’re providing a 12 million grant to the Government of Ecuador for this compact, which is going to benefit the electricity sector and your economy. And in the end, obviously the most important obligation any government has is the safety and security of their people. But upon that foundation is where you build the foundation of prosperity and economic opportunity. Ecuador actually has economic growth, and it’s pretty impressive given some of the things that are going on around the world. But they can do so much more if the security situation gets solved – and it is being solved very aggressively – and if we work together to pursue these opportunities to jointly develop our respective economies in ways that are mutually beneficial for both countries. So thank you very much. Muchísimas gracias . MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Thank you very much, Secretary. We would like to thank the presence of the authorities, the representatives of the press, and also of everybody that has been here with us today. We would like to specially request the press to please stay in your position until the authorities leave. Good afternoon, everybody, and thank you. title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori at a Joint Press Availability
text: hide Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori at a Joint Press Availability Remarks Marco Rubio, Secretary of State Keiko Fujimori, Peruvian President Presidential Palace Lima, Peru September 10, 2026 MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Welcome to the Túpac Amaru Hall of the Government Palace. Next, we will hear the remarks of the President of the Republic Keiko Sofía Fujimori Higuchi and the Secretary of State, His Excellency Marco Rubio. They will give their remarks after the meeting they held in the framework of the official meeting. Next, we’ll listen to the remarks by the President of the Republic, Ms. Keiko Sofía Fujimori. PRESIDENT FUJIMORI: (Via interpreter) Good morning, Secretary of State Mr. Marco Rubio, ministers, high officers, journalists. Your presence in Peru, Secretary Rubio, represents much more than an official visit. It symbolizes the meeting of two nations which for 200 years share the same view about freedom, independence, and sovereignty. Two hundred years ago Peru started to build its republic. The United States were already consolidating it. We were two young nations but with a very strong aspiration, that America could decide about its own destiny. Two hundred years have gone by and that vision is still in force, with different nuances, aspects, and new challenges, but with the same aim: that no external force takes away from us the possibility of living in freedom. For that reason, the first topic of our meeting has been how to face transnational organized crime, and we have talked about citizenship and security. As president of the Republic of Peru, I am happy to inform our nation that Peru will become part of the Shield of the Americas – (applause) – a multilateral coalition that includes more than 15 countries and which is led by the United States. Thank you, Secretary Rubio, for this opportunity because we have had to face terrorism and we know how difficult it is to face these criminal organizations that do not respect any borders. And for this reason, we need to join efforts with other countries. Being part of the Shield of the Americas will enable us, as we have already proved, to obtain faster information and act more firmly. And from Peru, we will act with all the powers granted by the law and the constitution. We have also had the chance to talk about the challenge posed by the El Niño phenomenon. We were sharing with Secretary Rubio that this phenomenon will begin, it was announced, in February; however, the previous government did not take pertinent actions. In the first days of August, as the press already knows, we began with the cleaning of the riverbeds and prepare ourselves for the emergency. And we would like to take the opportunity to thank the United States for the support that is being provided thanks to the coordinations of Ambassador Navarro. And we are thankful because in February 2027, the Comfort American ship will arrive to the coast of Peru. This is one of the largest hospital vessels of the world, with more than 1,000 beds and highly equipped technology. This will help the population of the northern part of our country. We thank for the assistance that could be given by the Southern Command and the support that we are already receiving from the DEA and the FBI and other federal agencies. We’ve been able to talk about many subjects – education, infrastructure investment, our trade exchange. But we salute today the political decision of President Trump to look at Latin America that Secretary Rubio is here in Peru because it shows the true value you’re giving to this bilateral relations. We’re talking about 200 years of friendship. Welcome, Secretary Rubio. (Applause.) MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) We thank the words of President of the Republic. Now we have the remarks from the Secretary of State, our Excellency Marco Rubio. SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) Thank you very much, dear President, for having a meeting. The cooperation that exists through the first 40 days of your administration has meant a lot. We’ve done a lot, but we will do more. I think that I come and I leave with a lot of confidence that the relations between our countries will start a very special era and will benefit both countries in a very important way. It’s important to have, like you’ve said, the relation for more than 200 years between our countries. We are a very, very young republic. You were starting as a republic; and we’ve done a lot during these 200 years, but we still have a lot to do. We are facing the modern threats, which are different from a decade ago, those new (inaudible) threats. Our obligation, the most important thing, is to achieve peace, to achieve security of the people. And when that is threatened, it’s impossible. It’s impossible to have economy growth, prosperity. It’s impossible to achieve other things if peace, calm, and order are not present. These are important things and are very necessary for economic growth and prosperity, which is all – what we want. Which is the biggest threat? The threat nowadays are transnational organized crime. Bear in mind that we had these groups operating within national territories only, but nowadays it is a network, it’s a terrorist network, a criminal network, which is very dangerous, operating through borders and multiple countries with liaisons. It’s a criminal infrastructure with banking, finance, and they’re trying to take this hemisphere. We cannot let this happen. The only way we can confront them is to be strong and confront them. This is why we’re very happy and – well, that you have been elected. People elected you because you promised to confront this, and we will provide the support. Why? Not only because of the friendship, because it’s only of our national interest. To have operating criminals operating in this hemisphere – it’s a direct threat not only for the Peruvian people, but as well for the United States. I’m very, very happy to listen to the announcement that you will be partner of the Shield of the Americas. A shield against what, people may wonder? A shield against these criminal bands, criminal groups, terrorist groups that are a direct threat to the sovereignty to our countries. When we are encountering criminal bands that have more money and best military equipment than the military themselves, that is not acceptable. And against that is the shield. This is why we have 14 countries working together – hopefully we will add more countries – to confront and defeat forever these elements. What can we do at the same time for security, prosperity? And this is why we will always seek trade opportunities to work together with your government and your country, to seek trade agreements that will benefit directly our people, and as well, the United States economy. And we have multiple possibilities. We have spoken about that today and we still have a lot to do. And we’re starting to work on those topics. So for us, it is an honor to be here with you today and to start this new era in the relations between Peru and the United States. I think we have the possibility in our hands to start a very important time, historical era, in terms of what we can achieve together. If I may please switch to English because I do have U.S. press covering this. (In English) (Inaudible) President Fujimori for receiving us here today. I truly believe that we are entering a new era in U.S.-Peru relations, a golden era in many ways, because her administration has the right ideas. In her first 40 days in office, we’ve already done many things together, and there’s so much more for us to do together. I remind everybody that the most important obligation of any government to its people is the security and the stability and the order in that country. And when that is threatened, nothing else is possible – not economic growth, not prosperity, not upward mobility. And in fact, we look at the criminality that exists and the terrorism that exists in this region today – and the people most victimized by it are working people, common people, who cannot defend themselves against these criminal elements. This is – this has always been a threat in this region. But it has become a new threat because these are now transnational threats. These are transnational terrorist organizations that do not respect sovereign borders and operate in multiple countries with the same aim and the same goal of exploiting countries and exploiting their people and harming them. And I’m very pleased to hear the announcement that Peru will be joining the Shield of the Americas. What is it a shield against? It is a shield against these threats to the sovereignty of these independent nations. It is a shield against these transnational criminal groups that, in many cases, have more money and better military equipment than the states. That is unacceptable, and the only way to defeat it is to confront it forcefully. And it’s the reason why President Fujimori was elected because she told the people of this country she would confront this threat and she would defeat it, and we will help her. We are going to help as we possibly can because it is in our national interest as well. Beyond that, there is extraordinary commercial opportunities. We’ve talked about some of those today. There are real opportunities to us to work together on commercial deals and commercial projects that are extraordinarily beneficial to Peru, to the people of Peru, but also beneficial to the people of the United States. That will be a core of our relationship as well. So it’s an honor to be here. It’s an honor to be with you. And I thank you and I thank your team for receiving us. I can’t wait to see the exciting things we’ll do together. Thank you. (Applause.) MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) We thank our Secretary of State for his remarks. Now we will take two questions per country for each authority. Please we’d like to invite the press. Start with the name of your organization. QUESTION: (Via interpreter) Good afternoon, President and Secretary of State. My first question is for you. What is the importance of this meeting that you have sustained with the Secretary of State, considering that this first official encounter with the United States of America? And number two, what is the importance that Peru becomes part of the Shield of the Americas, and how this will strengthen the security policy in favor of Peruvians? Thank you. PRESIDENT FUJIMORI: (Via interpreter) For Peru, it is of the essence – it is of the essence for Peru to know that the United States has now a political view of Latin America. We were speaking with Secretary Rubio that in previous administrations that importance was not given to the region. And his presence marks this difference – President Trump’s view. Entering the Shield of the Americas is of the essence for Peru. First of all, because it relaunches the joint work of both countries (inaudible) during the ‘90s. Let’s remember that the USA helped us in the fight against drug trafficking, and we were able to reduce the coca leaf production. In 1990 we had 120,000 hectares; that went down to 20,000 hectares. This reduction was possible with the work done with alternative crops, directly working with the farmers themselves. We have already shown results when two countries have a political decision, can work jointly shoulder to shoulder. Entering the Shield of the Americas will help us to obtain information. Peru confronted Shining Path and the MRTA, two terrorist groups, and was able to defeat them. And these two groups worked within Peruvian territory. Now criminal organizations know no borders. Some weeks ago it was possible to capture a criminal from the Los Pulpos criminal organization, and he was in Bolivia. This information was handed over to us through the FBI, and the Peruvian and Bolivian police were able to work jointly. For this reason it is of the essence to be part of the Shield of the Americas, because we will be able to act directly on our own behalf and on behalf of the cabinet of ministers led by Mr. Galarreta. We have the will to confront them, and with information from all countries we will be able to act faster and obtain specific and tangible results. QUESTION: Vera Bergengruen with The Wall Street Journal . Mr. Secretary, you have stressed that the members of the Shield of the Americas are sovereign partners. But if one of these governments refuses to act against one of these groups that Washington deems a terrorist threat, does the U.S. reserve the right to act unilaterally, including here in Peru? And President Fujimori: (Via interpreter) The question wanted more information about the partner of the Shield of the Americas. This will include to collaborate with the United States here in the country. SECRETARY RUBIO: I’ll answer that question in English to Spanish. I don’t know if you guys heard it. Basically, the gist of the question is, if you’re a member of the Shield and refuse to act, does the United States – will the United States act unilaterally? Well, if we were going to act unilaterally, why would we need the Shield? We’re not – if we were interested in acting unilaterally, we have the capacity to act unilaterally. The reason why we’re not doing it is because we want to do it with our partners. It’s the most effective way to do it. For us to confront transnational criminal groups, we need to do it inside the sovereign territory of countries, and we want to partner with those countries. It’s in their interest to do it. That is why we have the Shield. That is why the Shield exists. People make up these problems that don’t exist. They’re getting ahead of themselves with these – these ridiculous sort of things that no one’s even contemplating. The bottom line is the reason why we have a Shield is because we choose to act in partnership with our partners. So it’s very simple. This is not very complicated; let me explain this to you. It’s a very, very simple equation. We have a country that says we want to defeat these criminals, these terrorists, these evil, despicable human beings; we want to defeat them. We want to work with America to defeat them. And so we say, of course we want to work – what should we say to them? No, we don’t want to work with you? No, we’d like you not to do anything about these groups? We have a president here who has said very clearly – not to us, to the people of her country; it’s why they elected her – I am going to defeat these groups that extort you, I am going to defeat these groups that kill you, I am going to defeat these groups that terrorize your children in our communities. And the United States has said we’re so happy you’re doing that, it’s important for us as well, and we’re going to partner with you. That is the purpose of the Shield, to shield the region against this threat to the sovereignty of every one of our nations. (Via interpreter) The question was if the United States will act unilaterally if the member country of the Shield will not act. It’s a ridiculous question because if we’re going to do it unilaterally, then why would we have the Shield? The reason why we have the Shield is because we don’t want to act unilaterally. We want to act together. We want to act jointly. Why do we want it? It’s very simple. These are terrorist groups. Please be clear, these are not criminals stealing a bank. These are terrorist groups extorting people, extorting and doing a lot of – committing multiple crimes, things that you cannot even think about. They’re evil. So these – we need to defeat them, and we need to work together. When we see that there is a leader, a president that was elected with that promise to the people – and she is compliant with this; she will defeat and confront these groups – we will support her. Because it’s of our interest as well to work with you, of course, to your country or a sovereign country. And this is an enormous responsibility to confront these groups, and we will do our best to support to be able so she can comply with that promise. She will help us, but we will help them as well. This is how the partnerships work, this is how allies work, and this is what is the Shield. It is a powerful partnership against these diabolic groups that have terrorized the region for many, many years and through multiple leaders, and many, many, many political leaders from multiple countries don’t have the courage to confront them, or at many times they were involved. And this impunity will no longer be accepted, and this is what we are seeing, and in other countries as well that are a member of the Shield of the Americans. PRESIDENT FUJIMORI: (Via interpreter) I want to reflect on a question. When we requested powers, this request was filed with congress by the prime minister. We requested to declare these criminal groups as hostile and terrorist groups. This mechanism will be fundamental. Second of all, we want to coordinate and strengthen the justice administration system to face decisively these criminal organizations. All of these mechanisms will help us obtain information through the Shield of the Americas and the different government agencies. (In English) So we are extremely happy, and we are thankful for Peru to be part now of the Shield of the Americas. QUESTION: (Via interpreter) Ayrton Luera from ATV Noticias . My question was with this incorporation of Peru into Shield of Americas, Mr. Rubio, would be – will we expect military operations or emergency operations in Peruvian territory? And if so, Madam President, could you tell us about the conversations that have taken place, if these interventions respect Peruvian sovereignty? And Mr. Rubio, what would be your answer to this public response of the Chinese embassy after your column in the press? SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) I don’t know what the Chinese embassy said. I’m not here to talk about what the Chinese embassy said. So, but the first question that you asked, we’re going to be – this is a sovereign country. You have your laws, you have a process. It’s a democratic country. You have a system, government system, a legal system; you will comply to that. We’re willing to do all what we can to assist you. This is going to be based on the cooperation that you request. We don’t want to be less, offer less, but not offer more than what you’re requesting. We’ll work together with this government that has an interest in defeating and have an obligation it’s committed to confront and defeat these criminal groups. So we’re not going to do anything that is outside the legal framework of your country or outside what the government will request. (In English) The question was would we do anything in the country, military activities and the like – we’re not going do anything that our partners don’t ask us to do. This is a democracy. This is a republic. They have laws, they have a system of government, they have regulations, they have a process they have to go through. We are not – we don’t want to do less than what you ask of us, but we’re not going to do more than what you ask of us. We are partners and we are allies. That’s how partnerships and alliances work. PRESIDENT FUJIMORI: (Via interpreter) I wanted to mention that even before we entered the Shield of the Americas our police force was being trained by the FBI. Even Great Britain was assisting us in this training and in the strengthening of our police force. And with our entry into the Shield of Americas we will have a more solid position. With regard to the entry of troops, there is a special provision in the constitution. Every time there is this kind of entry, a special authorization is requested to the congress of the republic. Of course, we will uphold this rule. Peru’s sovereignty is intact. We will recover order, tranquility, and peace for all of the Peruvian people. For this reason, we thank Secretary Rubio for his presence and to be here to be able to announce that Peru will be part of the Shield of the Americas. Thank you so much. MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) We will now listen to the last question of this conference. QUESTION: Eric Martin with Bloomberg News. Secretary Rubio, as you get ready to conclude this three-day visit to Peru, Colombia, and Ecuador, what is your message to the people of the region about the benefits of partnering with the U.S. and to voters in neighboring Brazil as they face elections in one month from now in some of the same security and other challenges of countries in the region? And President Fujimori – Presidente Fujimori: (Via interpreter) After the visit of Secretary Rubio — SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) Oh, he spoke Spanish. You’re tricky. (In English) I didn’t know he spoke Spanish. (Via interpreter) I can no longer speak Spanish because he’ll know. (In English) I’m sorry. QUESTION: (Via interpreter) Thank you, Secretary. President Fujimori, after the visit of Secretary Rubio, after today, and after being six weeks in office, are you prepared to take more steps to associate and work with the United States despite the massive investment of China in Peru during the last years, including the Port of Chancay? Thank you. SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) Thank you. He speaks Spanish. I mean, I was – I’m no longer going to be able to speak Spanish in front of you. It’s a joke, obviously. First, what’s our message? Let’s be clear on this. I’ve said for more than 20 years, unfortunately, administrations of both political parties, they’ve ignored the region. The focus was on different parts of the world. If you study – because I have two jobs: Secretary of State and also I am a consultant to the national security for President Trump at the Security Council. So our National Security Strategy speaks very openly about we will give priority to this side of the hemisphere. Why? Because we’re part of it, because geography is real, and the problems of the hemisphere impacts directly. It doesn’t mean that other problems outside this hemisphere are not important, but what really happens here in South America, Central America, and the Caribbean has a direct impact to the United States. Number two, we have a lot of people in common. How many U.S. Americans come visit, have businesses here, are tourists, live here, and vice versa? We have very – a very strong bond we cannot ignore, so we’ll give the priority. And not rhetorically – because there has been other administrations, oh, no, yes, we are focused on the side of the hemisphere, but they are not doing things, they haven’t done things. We are going to be focusing. First, it’s important for us, Peru as a country, as part of our national interest. So this visit is not unexpected. I’ve done this visit as a senator, I’m doing this as the Secretary of State, and we will continue doing this type of visits, and we will have concrete efforts. It’s not just simply the Shield of the Americas. We’ll have other efforts jointly to confront the interests that we have in common with our friends and our allies. And we want all the time – this is the most important. This is very, very important in democracy. When a president is elected and the president decides to cooperate and work with the United States, it’s super important that we can show the people that there are benefits for the people to get a partnership with the United States and work together, not only at the security level but as well trade and economically speaking. And we need to try to do that, and we want to make sure that the countries that cooperate with us are going to be able to respond to their voters: This is the consequence, the result of our cooperation with the United States. (In English) Very briefly, the question was in English: What is our message? Our message is what we’ve been saying all along. We have a National Security Strategy. I helped write it. And it talks about how the Western Hemisphere is a priority for this administration – not a rhetorical priority, not a symbolic priority, not a ceremonial priority – a real priority. That’s why I’ve traveled extensively in the region, that’s why we’ve received visitors from the region, and that’s why we’re here today. Because geography is real. The things that happen in this hemisphere directly impact us. We’re not doing anybody a favor here. Us getting involved in the region is not a favor; it is essential to our own security, to our own prosperity, to our own well-being in the United States of America. And this administration is committed to this. And there’ll be more if – people talk about the Shield of the Americas. I’m very proud of it. There’s going to be more initiatives like that in multiple realms where we can work together. But for this administration, this hemisphere is a priority, and you will continue to see it demonstrated over and over and over again. PRESIDENT FUJIMORI: (Via interpreter) Peru is part of APEC, the Asian Pacific economic forum; the United States too. And Peru has a significant production of minerals, fish products, agricultural products, and we will continue with this effort of having trade exchanges with different countries from Asia, from the Pacific, and from Europe of course. But today, with the presence of Secretary Rubio and the agreement signed in recent days, and with this direct collaboration that will be reciprocal, we begin a new era of relations between Peru and the United States. And these relations will surely strengthen both countries. So thank you, Secretary Rubio, for your presence. We hope you can visit us again. And we have already talked about other dates where we will be able to exchange more ideas and re-establish this cooperation, bridges between both countries. Thank you. (Applause.) MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) We would like to thank the press for their questions, and we would like to invite President Fujimori and Secretary Rubio to step up for an official photograph. We hope that you can move forward to be able to capture this photo. This act has ended. Thank you for your presence. We wish you a good afternoon, and we will now like to request the Peruvian press to remain in your places while we wait for the other part of the press to leave. Thank you.
