title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Paraguayan Foreign Minister Rubén Ramírez Lezcano at the Signing of a Memorandum of Understanding for Strategic Civil Nuclear Cooperation
text: Home Office of the Spokesperson Press Releases … Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Paraguayan Foreign Minister Rubén Ramírez Lezcano at the Signing of a Memorandum of Understanding for Strategic Civil Nuclear Cooperation hide Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Paraguayan Foreign Minister Rubén Ramírez Lezcano at the Signing of a Memorandum of Understanding for Strategic Civil Nuclear Cooperation Remarks Marco Rubio, Secretary of State Colin L. Powell Treaty Room Washington, DC August 4, 2026 SECRETARY RUBIO: Before we sign it I just want to say a few words in English and Spanish. I think this is just another step in the continued growth of our relationship between our two countries. I think this MOU reflects that continued cooperation. In fact, as we were commenting in our meeting a moment ago, we’ve always had strong links between the United States and Paraguay; those links have only grown stronger. And agreements like this and others that I hope will happen in the future will begin to create real concrete progress, institutionalize the deep ties between our two countries moving forward so that they’re not just the product of one administration or one era but they become enduring and can survive the shifts in political winds that happen in democracies and in – from time to time. But nonetheless, the underpinnings in the foundation remain firm and strong. So very proud to be a part of this today and I think it’s a testament to that. SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) In Spanish, what I mean is that clearly the relationship between the United States and Paraguay has always been very close, and very, very strong. But what we have seen in the past year and a half has been incredible. The relationship between both countries has grown on a historic scale and today’s agreement is simply evidence of that. What we are aiming for is to establish a relationship that not only continues to grow, but that also becomes part of something permanent, so that regardless of the changes in government that may occur in the future —for example, in our system we see changes every 4 or 8 years—, the basis, the foundation of the relationship between both countries can survive any of the political changes that may take place in the future. I can tell you that we —obviously when I was a senator, I was very interested in the relationship between our country and Paraguay. But now in my role as Secretary of State, it is even easier for me to contribute to this effort. Based on what we can achieve in the next year and a half, and what we have achieved together over the past year and a half, which are not only bilateral issues but also regional issues, I think the relationship between the United States and Paraguay will change forever, in an extraordinary way. And today is evidence of that and represents one more step on that path that we have, that goal that we have in common. FOREIGN MINISTER LEZCANO: Really brilliant. I will start in English. Thank you so much, Marco, because we are working so close. Our strategic alliance is quite important for both countries. We are working on security, trade, investment. We are working not only at the level of bilateral cooperation and security, we are working the whole month on the security cooperating in our region but also globally. That is that we share values and principles – freedom, democracy, human rights, rule of law – that allow us to work very close together. I would like to think, through this agreement today, we are still deepening our cooperation. And thank you so much, Marco, because your work is quite hard for us. (In Spanish.) SECRETARY RUBIO: Okay. FOREIGN MINISTER LEZCANO: Let’s sign. (The Memorandum of Understanding was signed.) (Applause.) SECRETARY RUBIO: Do I leave it here? STAFF: Yes. QUESTION: Mr. Secretary, quick question. I’m sure you saw a Newsweek cover saying what Trump got right in Venezuela. And we want to know when we expect elections in Venezuela. SECRETARY RUBIO: It’s a process, and they have to have them. Obviously, there’s a lot of work that has to happen to lay the groundwork for an election. As I said, you have to have true freedom of the press. You have to have multiparty participation. You have to have national reconciliation. I mean, you have to have an electoral commission that will accurately count the votes. So it has to happen and it’s a work in progress, but again, it’s been about six months since Maduro was removed, and there’s a lot going on at the same time with economics and so forth. So I think we’re moving on two tracks. We want to improve the daily lives – help improve the daily lives of Venezuelans economically so that they’re better off, they’re more prosperous. I think that helps as well facilitate the political transition. And you also have to have a process where every element of political society in Venezuela has a role to play, not just in constructing elections but constructing the government and future of the country. So I think it’s going to require some persistence and a little bit of patience – not years, but certainly months and weeks. It’s going to take some time to get there. You’re dealing with a system that’s been in place now for almost three decades, so it’s not going to be from one day to the next. If you look at the transitions in Eastern Europe, after the fall of the Iron Curtain; if you look at Paraguay, a country that undertook a transition from authoritarianism to democracy, it took them almost three and a half years to complete that process. These things are difficult. They don’t happen – I know we are – I know we are all used to instant results or at least expectations of instant results, but if you want to do it right, what you want to have is a democratic transition that happens that brings society together, where there’s a national reconciliation, where you have political parties that are able to openly and freely participate, where you have an electoral count but you also have an economy and a country whose institutions are functioning so that they’re not inheriting a disaster, they’re not inheriting the reconstruction process, they’re inheriting a functional state. So all of that is to say that these things don’t happen from one day to the next, but the needle is pointing in the right direction. And even though the progress is probably slower than all of us would want, there is progress and progress will happen, and we’re committed to it. Okay? Thank you. QUESTION: Secretary, can you speak about the latest on Iran and whether we’re close to reaching a deal? We’ve seen the messaging from the Qataris about their mediation. Do you – how do you see the possibilities of a deal with Iran and with their talks — SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, I think there’s two things to talk about when there’s a deal. There’s the big deal, which is the one that has to do with their nuclear ambitions. They can never have a nuclear weapon; the President’s been clear about that. So the denuclearization of Iran is the ultimate deal. I think the immediate deal and the one that you’ve seen a lot of focus on is the straits. The straits – there are ships moving through the straits, there are oil – there is oil moving right now through the straits. So the straits are open. Nonetheless, I think that there is a conversation and a negotiation that we are involved in between Oman and Iran on how more ships can be able to go through their safely in the short term as we move towards these longer-term talks about denuclearization. And suffice it to say there’s been progress made in those talks but not finality yet. We’re hoping that will happen very shortly. Okay? Thank you guys. FOREIGN MINISTER LEZCANO: Thank you so much. title: Opening Remarks at the Second Pax Silica Summit
text: Home Under Secretary for Economic Affairs Remarks & Releases … Opening Remarks at the Second Pax Silica Summit hide Opening Remarks at the Second Pax Silica Summit Remarks Jacob Helberg, Under Secretary for Economic Affairs (E) June 25, 2026 Good morning. Ministers, ambassadors, distinguished delegates, industry leaders, and friends— Welcome to the second Pax Silica Summit. When we gathered for the first Pax Silica Summit last December, we shared a simple conviction: that trusted partners should work together to build the foundations of the AI economy. Today, it is remarkable to see how much that vision has grown. It is a pleasure to welcome all of you to Washington, and I want to extend a warm welcome to the many countries joining the Pax Silica community for the first time. Just a few months ago, Pax Silica was an idea shared among a small group of partners. Today, it has grown into a coalition representing more than thirty governments and economies, including the observer nations joining us today. The enthusiasm for this effort reflects a shared recognition that artificial intelligence will not only shape the future of technology—it will shape the future of economic growth, competitiveness, and prosperity. Governments everywhere are asking many of the same questions: How do we build trusted AI ecosystems? How do we attract investment? How do we secure resilient supply chains? How do we ensure our citizens share in the prosperity AI can create? No country can answer those questions alone. Countries are not looking for another forum to manage decline. They are looking for practical partners to help build growth. That is exactly why we are here today. Artificial intelligence is already transforming the global economy, but what we have seen so far is only the beginning. AI is not just a powerful driver of growth today — it will be one of the defining engines of prosperity for decades to come. But AI is about far more than frontier models. It requires compute. It requires abundant, reliable energy. It requires semiconductors. It requires critical minerals. It requires trusted connectivity. It requires resilient supply chains, world-class talent, and investment. If the twentieth century was powered by oil and steel, the twenty-first century will be powered by compute, energy, and the infrastructure that makes artificial intelligence possible. Across the AI ecosystem, we also see tremendous opportunities. There are inefficiencies in how trusted countries move critical goods. There are shortages of talent. There are gaps in infrastructure and investment. There are opportunities to strengthen supply chains and remove unnecessary barriers to innovation. These are not challenges that any one country can solve alone. They are opportunities that trusted partners can tackle together. That is why Pax Silica exists. Pax Silica is designed to be an action platform — not another international bureaucracy. It is a practical toolkit that enables trusted partners to solve problems together, pilot new ideas, and scale what works. Today’s announcements reflect how quickly this partnership has evolved, from dialogue to delivery. So today, we are excited to roll out a series of practical, replicable initiatives that countries across this partnership can adopt, adapt, and build upon. Joint Statement On AI Opportunity First, many of our governments will sign the Joint Statement on AI Opportunity Partnership, a shared commitment to pro-growth AI policies, trusted technology ecosystems, resilient supply chains, and investment in the infrastructure needed to power the AI economy. The Joint Statement reflects a simple but important idea: governments should not approach AI primarily through the lens of restriction. We should approach it through the lens of opportunity. Innovation, entrepreneurship, investment, and technological leadership remain the surest path to broad-based prosperity. Pax Pass Working with Congress, I’m excited to announce a new Pax Silica Artificial Intelligence Assistance Project for Pax partners that ship high-value AI supply chain products through Panama. We will launch Pax Pass, an ambitious new platform that has the potential to transform how trusted partners move the critical goods that power the AI economy. By combining cargo verification, AI-powered risk assessment, and pre-approved expedited processing for trusted shipments, Pax Pass will reduce friction, strengthen supply-chain resilience, and accelerate trusted trade. To support this effort, the Department of State is working with Congress to commit $50 million in foreign assistance funding dedicated to the development and deployment of Pax Pass. We are putting our resources behind our vision and demonstrating that trusted partnership is backed by real investment. Foundry School We will also launch Foundry School, a workforce development initiative built in partnership with Stanford University to equip entrepreneurs, engineers, and advanced manufacturing leaders across Pax Silica economies. This partnership is formalized in a Memorandum of Understanding, signed by myself and Stanford President Jonathan Levin. I am grateful to President Levin, and to the Stanford professors and administrators who will make Foundry School a reality. Foundry School will begin with a seminar series at Stanford, gathering the greatest luminaries of advanced manufacturing to teach the principles behind the world’s most successful industrial enterprises. In parallel, Stanford and the State Department will develop a first-of-its-kind curriculum for institutions across Pax Silica economies to adopt and teach. Advanced manufacturing is not yet well established as a standalone field of study, yet few things matter more to national power and economic strength. Foundry School will give the next generation of technologists and industrial leaders a shared foundation in the capabilities that underwrite prosperity and security. Economic Security Zone And we will announce the first Economic Security Zone in the Philippines — a model designed to attract investment, expand trusted manufacturing capacity, and create innovation-friendly environments that generate long-term growth. Our hope is that this is only the first of many such zones across the Pax Silica network, creating a connected ecosystem where investment, innovation, and trusted production reinforce one another across partner countries. These are not isolated projects. They are practical, replicable pilots designed to help countries solve common challenges together. Taken together, these initiatives invite a broader question: What is the best path to prosperity in the AI age? There are different answers emerging around the world. Some governments have embraced the concept of digital sovereignty or the belief that countries should seek to build and control every layer of the technology stack within their own borders. We believe there is a better path. The real measure of sovereignty in the AI age is not the ability to recreate yesterday’s technologies. It is the ability to contribute to tomorrow’s breakthroughs. That is innovation sovereignty. Innovation sovereignty means creating the conditions for entrepreneurs to build, researchers to discover, companies to invest, workers to thrive, and trusted partners to specialize, collaborate, and compete together at the technological frontier. That is the vision reflected in the AI Opportunity Statement. And that is the vision behind Pax Silica. Thank you for your leadership, your partnership, and your willingness to build that future together. Welcome to the second Pax Silica Summit. title: U.S. Concludes $302 Million Security Cooperation Loan to Albania, Advancing Military Modernization and Strengthening European Defense
text: Home Bureau of Political-Military Affairs Remarks & Releases … U.S. Concludes $302 Million Security Cooperation Loan to Albania, Advancing Military Modernization and Strengthening European Defense hide U.S. Concludes $302 Million Security Cooperation Loan to Albania, Advancing Military Modernization and Strengthening European Defense Media Note Bureau of Political-Military Affairs August 3, 2026 Today, the United States is proud to announce Albania’s ratification and signing of a new $302 million Foreign Military Financing (FMF) loan that will support Albania’s progress towards meeting The Hague Defense Commitment of spending 5 percent of GDP on defense by 2035. The FMF loan will help modernize Albania’s armed forces by supporting the procurement of key U.S. origin capabilities and strengthen Europe’s ability to lead on its own defense. As a NATO ally, Albania has closely aligned with the United States on critical foreign policy issues, including as a founding member of President Trump’s Board of Peace. For additional information, please contact the Bureau of Political-Military Affairs’ Office of Congressional and Public Affairs at T_Outreach_PM@state.gov . title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio On Fox News Channel’s My View with Lara Trump
text: Home Office of the Spokesperson Press Releases … Secretary of State Marco Rubio On Fox News Channel’s My View with Lara Trump hide Secretary of State Marco Rubio On Fox News Channel’s My View with Lara Trump Interview Marco Rubio, Secretary of State The White House Washington, D.C. July 28, 2026 QUESTION: Secretary, great to have you back. Thank you so much. SECRETARY RUBIO: Glad to be back. It’s been a while. QUESTION: Yeah. There’s so much to talk about, but I want to start with Cuba. SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah. QUESTION: This has been of particular interest to the State Department right now. You guys released a 100-page report on Cuba, calling it, “The Capital of 21st Century Communism.” And this report talks about the fact that Cuba’s goal essentially is to erase the United States from the Earth. It also details a Cuban spy network that’s been undermining American interests. How did we get to a place where Cuba has become so much of a threat – it feels like again – to the United States? SECRETARY RUBIO: I think for those who have followed the issue of Cuba, this is not unfamiliar to us. But to the average American, you see Cuba, a small country 90 miles off our shores, nine and a half million people population. But people forget that when it comes to things like espionage and influence operations, they actually are an influence and espionage superpower. If you look at the history of espionage in the United States, Cuba is the only country that consistently has implanted and embedded spies in our system without even paying them. We had an ambassador, a U.S. ambassador, who ended up being a Cuban spy and was recently convicted. We’ve had them penetrate the highest levels of the Defense Intelligence Agency. Ana Belén Montes was one of the single biggest intelligence failures on the part of the United States and one of the biggest penetrations we ever had in our system. So – and then on the influence front, if you look all throughout Latin America, every communist left-wing insurgency that’s destabilized governments across the region, every single one of them over the last 40, 50 years has found its support, its help, in many cases its birth, from a Cuban influence operation. So, it was an important report just to highlight the role they play in our country, a very negative role. QUESTION: The report also links Cuban influence to the rise in Antifa, the riots that we saw in 2020, as well as the surge of radical activism that we’ve seen all over these college campuses. To the average person, those things, I think, feel generally organic, but it turns out there are a lot of different powers – Cuba being one of them – that are influencing all of these things day to day. SECRETARY RUBIO: It’s the same network of protesters around the country. They were the same people you saw on the streets burning things in 2020. They then flip it around and they become the pro-Hamas protesters, then they flip it around and within 48 hours of Maduro’s arrest have preprinted signs outside the courthouse demanding his release. And then they’re out there doing the ICE stuff, attacking ICE agents. There’s nothing organic about it. It is funded, it is organized, and Cuba is a part of that network, and in some cases a critical part of that network. And it’s a network they will weaponize against us, and they talk about it openly, about how they will use that network to pressure American policymakers – not just here in the United States, like Code Pink, but all over the world. QUESTION: Critics of this report, of course, are saying, oh, well, these are scare tactics to potentially justify some U.S. military action against Cuba. It sounds like this is something we should take seriously, and this report sounds very real. SECRETARY RUBIO: Everything in there is factual. And frankly, I don’t think they can dispute it. People can argue that we shouldn’t do with it, and I know there are plenty of people in American academia – and frankly in American press – that sympathize with the Cuban regime and have for a very long time. Part of it is motivated by their anti-Americanism, and part of it is motivated by ideological affinity. There are plenty – there are enough people in key nodes of our society, including professors, but frankly, in the past we’ve seen people within our own government, that sympathize with the Cuban regime. It’s the way they get spies without paying them. But it doesn’t mean we can ignore this threat. Put aside for a moment my history, the fact that I’m Cuban American, the fact that I grew up in Miami. This is 90 miles from our shores. A failed state 90 miles from our shores that happens to be aligned with adversaries to the United States is a national security threat to our country. QUESTION: I want to move quickly to Venezuela. The interim government and opposition leaders there are taking steps towards a possible future with democratic elections. What role is the United States currently playing, and what can you tell us about Venezuela? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, the first thing about Venezuela is I know we’re not in the era of patience and persistence, but these things take time. You’re dealing with a system that’s been in place for over a quarter-century, so those are deep roots that you have to deal with. It’s also a country that faces a lot of problems, I mean a lot of economic problems, not to mention now they’ve had an earthquake. So, that’s why we’ve always talked about phase one, where our priority was stabilization. We didn’t want the country devolving into civil war, mass migration, civil unrest, and so forth. Step two is a recovery phase, which I think we’re into. Obviously, the earthquake adds complexity to it. You’ve got to have a functioning economy. You need to have laws and rules and regulations in place so that investors from America and around the world can go in and safely invest and create prosperity. Ultimately, you have to have transition. At some point in time there has to be legitimate elections at every level so that people know that the government that’s there is a legitimate government chosen by their people. Step one towards that is a national reconciliation. This is a people that have been divided politically for a very long time against each other, and you’re going to have to look at models like what you saw happen in Eastern Europe after the fall of the Soviet Union. I think the role the U.S. Government can continue to play is as a facilitator of all of this. QUESTION: You’ve been outspoken for many years about the threat from China. President Xi, of course, is going to come visit here in Washington, D.C., in September. You’ve had to sit across the table, though, from China’s foreign minister. You’ve had to negotiate and talk on America’s behalf. How have you found, in this role, negotiating with Beijing? SECRETARY RUBIO: On the one hand, all the things that China wants to become the most powerful country in the world, and they want to do so at our expense. Obviously, we are Americans; we’re not going to allow that to happen. At the same time, they are the two most powerful economies in the world, probably the two most powerful militaries in the world, though ours is further along than theirs, but nonetheless. And I think it’s important for two big countries like this, the two most powerful countries in the world, have to have a relationship, have to have the ability to speak to one another and try to deconflict where possible, because it could lead to some really bad things. The foundation of that is the relationship that President Trump has with President Xi, which is a relationship of mutual respect and they get along. And that really is important that our two presidents can speak to one another, and it’s okay. I think it’s almost irresponsible, by the way, to not have direct communications with the Chinese. We want stability in our relationship. Both sides, I think, recognize that there are areas where we’re not going to agree, and including areas where we’re going to have to compete. Now, there are areas we can work together on. That’s phenomenal, fantastic for the world. But I think there’s going to be a lot of areas of friction and competition, and we have to manage that at the same time as we have to have a relationship with them, but we always have to look out for what’s best for America. QUESTION: Well, it seems like China has been on their best behavior knowing that President Trump is in the White House, but a lot of people believe that they may just be biding their time in terms of possibly taking over Taiwan. What do you say to that? SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, I can’t speak 20 or 30 years from now. I can say that our position is we support – we don’t support any change to the current status quo that exists there right now. We would be against any sort of compelled or coerced change in status. That point was made very clear in our meetings with the Chinese. Obviously, they have a very different point of view; it’s a very sensitive issue for them. So, again, it’s part of that delicate balancing act. Because look, any conflict between the U.S. and China, be it economic or be it military, God forbid, would be catastrophic for both countries and for the world. So, we have to manage that, but we can’t walk away or forfeit our national interests. So, this is the hard work of foreign policy, and it requires every administration to sort of balance these two competing tugs against us. QUESTION: Well, we hear a lot about tensions with China. We hear a lot about tensions with Russia, with Iran daily. I think Americans probably at some point get very overwhelmed because, unfortunately, the good stuff doesn’t make it out there often enough. What would you say, though, about the stability of the world right now given you’re in your position and the President is who he is? SECRETARY RUBIO: I think the world has always been complicated and tricky. I think the difference now is if something happens halfway around the world in a place you’ve never heard about before, and it’s really dramatic, you’re going to hear about it almost instantaneously. I think the world is also going through a period of rapid transformation. I mean, there is clearly a geopolitical reordering that is occurring, and I’ve talked about this repeatedly. We are – after the end of the Cold War, everybody thought the whole world was just going to become free-enterprise democracies and everyone would get along and nation-states would no longer matter. And unfortunately, we made decisions in our foreign policy on that ridiculous basis that actually caused us to hurt our country. We started saying things like we don’t care where things are made, let it be made in another country as long as it’s cheaper prices for America. And it ended up deindustrializing our country and costing us millions of jobs. So, what you see President Trump doing now is rebalancing those things on the economy using tariffs, on geopolitics using our presence in the world, especially in the Western Hemisphere, our own area neighborhood that we live in. And then of course there are legacy threats like the Iranian threat of a nuclear program, which can never happen. The President’s been very clear about that. So, you have all the old threats plus the emerging new ones, and they’re all happening at the same time, and they’re happening faster than they ever have before. And it’ll be the work of this administration, but it’ll be the work of future administrations. Some of these things are going to take decades to work themselves out. (Break.) QUESTION: And we’re back with more of our exclusive sit-down with Secretary of State Marco Rubio as the ongoing conflict in Iran remains top of mind for the American people. SECRETARY RUBIO: I don’t think the Iranian regime has ever faced a president like President Trump, which is someone that actually takes action. They got used to for 20 or 30 years not just the U.S. but the broader world allowing them to get away with things like lying, breaking deals, tricking people into agreements, and so forth. In this particular case, it was pretty straightforward. Iran wants a nuclear weapon, and they were building a conventional missile shield that they were going to hide behind. In essence, they wanted to be in a position a year and a half from now to be able to say: We have so many drones and so many missiles, you can’t possibly defend against them. That’s the place they wanted to get to. President Trump said we’re not – I’m not going to let you get to that place, and he went after – wiped out their navy, wiped out their air force, wiped out their missile defenses, wiped out their launchers, wiped out their factories that make all of these things, and severely degraded their defense capabilities. Now, they still have missiles and they still have drones and they can still do damage, but they no longer have that shield, that conventional shield that they could hide behind, and that’s changed the whole dynamic. It’s the only reason why they are now willing and in some cases seem eager to do a deal on denuclearization, to do a deal on the straits. Because we’re now approaching them from a position of strength, not from a position of weakness, which is what they perceived from previous administrations and, frankly, from the world writ large. QUESTION: The regime change has never been the goal, though. As you say, it has been denuclearization. Can you have one without the other, though? SECRETARY RUBIO: I think what does – the regime has to change. You might not have a regime change, but the regime has to change. The Iranian regime traditionally has been expeditionary. In essence, their view is they don’t want to just govern Iran; they want to govern the region. They view them – they want to export the revolution. That does have to change, and the only way you’re going to change that is if you make the price of it too high for them to be able to pay. QUESTION: The fact that so many of these Gulf Arab nations have all kind of aligned against Iran, that must be important. SECRETARY RUBIO: I would say two things about the Middle East and the Gulf – I mean, they’ve always understood who Iran was and the threat they posed. That threat has now become reality. They have now seen Iranian drones and Iranian missiles launched into their cities and against their energy infrastructure. The other thing that’s changed is I think you’re going to see more and more energy diversifying outside of the Straits of Hormuz, because from a geographic standpoint Iran will always be on the straits, whether they’re governed by this regime or a future government. But that’s going to be two permanent features that are going to emerge from this: You’re going to see the realignment in how energy flows, less reliant on the Straits of Hormuz; and you’re going to countries in the region that are no longer – now understand that Iran is no longer a theoretical threat. As long as this clerical regime remains in place, they are a real threat and a direct threat to their – not just to their economic interests but their security interests. QUESTION: Well, President Trump says he is going to confront Valdimir Putin regarding reports that Russia helped Iran target U.S. bases. How much does that relationship concern you? SECRETARY RUBIO: With Russia? QUESTION: Between Russia and Iran. SECRETARY RUBIO: Look, unfortunately, I think you’ll find in the world that there are countries, or at least companies within countries, that work with adversaries of ours. And when we identify it, we raise it, and in some cases very successfully. Nothing we have wanted to do in the Middle East – none of the actions we’ve taken, none of our successes – have in any way been impeded by anything that any other country in the world did against us. There are things that might be irritants, there are things that might be concerning, but there is nothing any other country is doing that in any way is standing in the way of us achieving the things we want to achieve or the objectives we want. QUESTION: Just to finish with the situation in Russia and Ukraine, is there anything at this point that the U.S. can realistically do to help bring talks together, bring this to an end? SECRETARY RUBIO: The President has made very clear if United States can play a role in bringing about an end to that war, we’re going to continue to explore it. We spent a lot of time on it in the first year. There came a point where it got to, like, stalemate, but we always stood willing and ready to play a constructive role. We’re the only country in the world, and President Trump’s the only leader in the world, that can bring the Russian side and the Ukrainian side to begin to talk about how you end it. The reality is that dynamics have changed just a little bit in that conflict over the last few months. The Ukrainians now are able to conduct long-range strikes deep into Russia, bringing the war toward – to the Russian people. What we are willing to explore is whether that new dynamic has in any way opened the door to some negotiated settlement. I know there’s going to be – you’re going to see some efforts over the next few weeks to see if we can’t restart talks between the two sides and bring this war to an end. But we also understand that both sides have some pretty strong red lines; and until we can bring those red lines a little closer together, we’re not going to be there yet. But we’re ready to go, and the President’s told his team if you see an opportunity to be a force that brings about some momentum behind peace talks, let’s do it. So, he always prefers diplomacy over war and peace over combat. QUESTION: Americans have seen so many versions of you, I think. We know Senator Rubio, we know candidate Rubio, now Secretary Rubio. Have you changed throughout the course of all of these different kind of phases of your life? And how do you think the American people’s perception of you has changed? Because you are memes everywhere – I think everybody loves to see all the different sides of you. SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, well, the meme thing, it was interesting because when it first came out, I hated that picture. (Laughter.) Because what happened is in that couch, if you don’t have a pillow behind your back, you kind of sink. So, I looked at the picture; I said, oh, this is terrible, I looked like whatever. And then it turned into this other thing. And it was fine, and it’s funny. I don’t really follow it very closely, but people have shown me pictures out there. We have a good friend here that works at the White House, Dan Scavino, made a nice board for me. (Laughter.) And even since he made that board, we had to update it, so – of all the different pictures. So that stuff is funny. You asked me if you’ve changed. I think everybody – you go through life, right? And as you go through life you learn new things, you see things you hadn’t seen before, you hear things you haven’t heard before. Certainly, I am a different person at 55 than I was at 25 or even 35 because I have 20 and 30 years of experience in between – in life and in work – that inform that. I think at your core you always want to remain the same person, though, right? And that is what are your priorities in life and what are the values that sort of drive you to do what you do, and I hope that hasn’t changed. And by the way, the world changes too. There are things that are true today that weren’t true 10 years ago. So, I think that – that’s true for all of us, not just me. QUESTION: I feel like you’ve been busier than ever. You’ve been traveling all over the place. But you’re doing all of that while being a husband, while being a father. Maybe talk about how that is, because I know for every kind of working parent out there, working spouse, it’s hard to take time, but I am sure your family keeps you very active. SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, it is, and I’m in an interesting season in life. For most of my time in public service, I had very young children or children that were still growing up. Now all four of my children are adults. My youngest graduated high school this year. I have a 26-year-old, a 24-year-old, a 21-year-old, and an 18-year-old. So, they have lives. They don’t just have – when you’re 15 or 16, you have opinions. When you get to 20, 24, 26, you have lives and you have stuff going on. I still look back at the time that they were young and wish I could have one more day with them when they were little, but you also appreciate the moment you live in. And then as far as being a husband, I think what’s happened is, because your kids are a little older and they have more time doing their own things, whether their school or their career, you spend more time with your – you almost, like, get back to where you were when you first started dating in some ways. So, you get to spend more time with my wife and sort of rediscover. So, it’s the second phase of that relationship, I guess, after all these years. So it’s an interesting season in life that I think we’re – mixing with what we’re doing here now – and find it pretty fulfilling and pretty happy. QUESTION: Well, when you go home, I’m curious: What is the first thing you do when Marco Rubio gets home? Do you sleep? What happens? SECRETARY RUBIO: (Laughter.) No, not when I get home. I don’t go right to sleep. Of course not. Usually, I mean, if you can – you really can’t in this job, and you certainly can’t working for this administration and this President, who never stops working, but I think it is good to try to disconnect for some period of time from your job or from your work. It could be watching a sporting event, it could be watching a movie, just anything that allows you to sort of disconnect and play the reset button. It’s harder – it was a lot easier to do that when you’re a senator. It’s much harder when you’re in this role and in this job, because the world isn’t going to stop and wait for you. Like, you may want – you may have made a plan tonight to watch a movie, but in the middle of that movie something blows up somewhere in the world, and you’ve got to know about it and you may have to do something about it. So, it’s harder, but it’s not forever, and it’s fulfilling to be in that role. QUESTION: So, if you could get a full week off without having anyone access you, what would you do? SECRETARY RUBIO: If I had a full week off, I’d be wondering what was going on. I’m being honest, and maybe that’ll change when I’m out of this job. But if I could – like, if I could make the world stop for a minute and have nothing going on, I’d love to – QUESTION: Yeah, (inaudible). SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, my wife’s going to hate this answer, but I’d love to sit down and, like, watch, like, every college football game starting at noon Eastern until one – when the West Coast games end at 2:00 a.m. our time Eastern. I’d love to be able to do that at least one weekend. I doubt I’ll be able to do that anytime soon. QUESTION: Okay. Final question: Is this going to be the Miami Dolphins season? What do we think? SECRETARY RUBIO: No. QUESTION: (Laughter.) SECRETARY RUBIO: No, they’re in massive rebuilding mode, but I think the needle is pointing in the right direction, but they need a couple years to rebuild that roster. QUESTION: Okay. We’re always looking to future seasons. SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, that’s right. QUESTION: Well, Secretary Marco Rubio, you are great. SECRETARY RUBIO: Thank you. QUESTION: Thanks for all you do for our country, and thank you so much for your time. SECRETARY RUBIO: Thank you. Thank you. title: Spain: Travel Advisory Updated to Raise Ceuta to Level 3
text: Home Office of the Spokesperson Press Releases … Spain: Travel Advisory Updated to Raise Ceuta to Level 3 hide Spain: Travel Advisory Updated to Raise Ceuta to Level 3 Media Note Office of the Spokesperson August 1, 2026 The Department of State updated its Travel Advisory for Spain on August 1, 2026, to raise Ceuta to Level 3 – Reconsider Travel due to unrest. The massive and uncontrolled arrival of migrants from Morocco to Ceuta may lead to unpredictable and dangerous security situations. Spain has deployed the Spanish military, Spanish National Police, and Guardia Civil as a result of this serious situation. Americans should reconsider travel to the area given the risks posed to their safety and security. The overall Travel Advisory level for Spain remains at Level 2 – Exercise Increased Caution. This replaces the previous Travel Advisory issued on May 12, 2025. The full text of the new Travel Advisory is as follows: There were no changes to the advisory level or risk indicators. A risk area was added. Advisory summary was updated. Travel Advisory – Spain Level 2 – Exercise Increased Caution Also includes areas at level 3 Exercise increased caution in Spain due to terrorism and unrest. Reconsider travel to Ceuta due to unrest. Advisory summary Terrorist groups continue plotting possible attacks in Spain. Terrorists may attack with little or no warning and target: Tourist locations Transportation centers like airports and train stations Markets and shopping malls Local government facilities Hotels, clubs, and restaurants Places of worship and educational institutions Parks Major sporting and cultural events Demonstrations are common. They may take place in response to political or economic issues, on politically significant holidays, and during international events. Risks in specific Areas: Level 3: Reconsider Travel Ceuta Reconsider Travel to Ceuta due to unrest. The massive and uncontrolled arrival of migrants from Morocco to Ceuta may lead to unpredictable and dangerous security situations. Spain has deployed the Spanish military, Spanish National Police, and Guardia Civil as a result of this serious situation. Americans should reconsider travel to the area given the risks posed to their safety and security. If you decide to travel to Spain: Avoid demonstrations and crowds. Be aware of your surroundings. Follow the instructions of local authorities. Check local media for breaking events. Be prepared to adjust your plans. U.S. citizens should always exercise caution when traveling abroad. Use these general tips to stay safe: Visit the CDC page for the latest Travel Health Information related to your travel. Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) to receive messages and alerts from the U.S. Embassy and make it easier to locate you in an emergency. Review the Country Security Report for Spain . Prepare a contingency plan for emergency situations. Review the International Travel Checklist . title: Additions to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List
text: Home Office of the Spokesperson Press Releases … Additions to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List hide Additions to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List Press Statement Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesperson July 31, 2026 Today, the United States added 43 companies based in China to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) Entity List, a key tool in preventing the importation into the United States of goods made with forced labor and leveling the playing field for American companies. The UFLPA, enacted in 2021, aims to prevent goods tainted by forced labor of Uyghurs and other ethnic minorities in China from entering the U.S. market, holding accountable entities involved in such practices. The newly listed entities are connected to the production and sale of goods made in Xinjiang or with the forced labor of Uyghurs and other groups specified in the UFLPA, and include seafood, gold, copper, transportation infrastructure, aluminum, tomatoes, cotton, garments, and frozen food, among others. These additions bring the total number of entities on the UFLPA Entity List to 187. Forced labor distorts markets and allows foreign actors to abuse the global trading system. Through the expansion of the UFLPA Entity List, the Trump Administration is taking action to eliminate forced labor from global supply chains, restoring a fair market for Americans while reducing instances of forced labor worldwide. The United States expects our trading partners around the world to enact and enforce similar laws prohibiting goods made with forced labor. Today’s action is being taken by the Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force (FLETF), a task force of interagency partners dedicated to monitoring the enforcement of the prohibition on importing goods made wholly or in part with forced labor into the United States, including as mandated by the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act. Chaired by the Department of Homeland Security, FLETF’s voting members include the Departments of State, Labor, Commerce, Justice, and Treasury, and the U.S. Trade Representative. For details, please refer to the Department of Homeland Security’s Press Release . title: Statement by Members of the High-Level Mission of OAS Member States to Bolivia
text: Home Office of the Spokesperson Press Releases … Statement by Members of the High-Level Mission of OAS Member States to Bolivia hide Statement by Members of the High-Level Mission of OAS Member States to Bolivia Media Note Office of the Spokesperson July 30, 2026 The text of the following statement will be released by the Governments of the United States of America, Argentina, Canada, Chile, Panama, Peru, and Uruguay. At the invitation of the Government of the Plurinational State of Bolivia and pursuant to the resolution adopted by the General Assembly of the Organization of American States, members of the High-Level Mission traveled to La Paz and Santa Cruz de la Sierra on July 29-30. We thank the Government of Bolivia, Foreign Minister Fernando Aramayo, members of Bolivia’s civil society, and all participants for their hospitality and engagement. While we respect the right to peaceful protest, we are deeply concerned by the impact of violent blockades on the lives of Bolivian citizens, democracy, and the rule of law in Bolivia. The continued efforts to undermine and overthrow the legitimate and democratically elected government of President Rodrigo Paz represent a serious threat to constitutional order and democratic stability in the country and our hemisphere. A minority acting outside the law attempted to disregard the will expressed by the majority of Bolivians at the polls less than one year ago, rejected the government’s willingness to engage in dialogue, and maintained road blockades for more than seven weeks, depriving the Bolivian people of access to food, health care, and other necessities such as fuel. These actions severely affected the daily lives of millions of citizens and put fundamental rights at risk. Deaths of Bolivian civilians occurred due to restrictions on free transit, which prevented them from accessing medicines, hospitals, or health centers in a timely manner. Protesters injured police officers in the line of duty. For any democracy to function, violence cannot subvert the constitutional order. We value the government’s willingness to engage in dialogue and in finding agreements. We express solidarity and support the constitutionally elected Bolivian government and urge the prioritization of dialogue and negotiations within the established constitutional framework as a fundamental tool of democracy. We urge peaceful resolution of conflicts without violence. Defending freedom, democracy, and hemispheric security requires commitment and cooperation. During this Mission, we reaffirm our commitment to continue working to strengthen stability and preserve the democratic order in our region and stand in solidarity with Bolivia’s democratic government and the people of Bolivia. We call for peaceful coexistence through consensus-building and dialogue. This statement reflects the experiences of the members of the Mission, who will report their findings to their respective governments, consult with other OAS member states on actionable items to support the democratically elected government of Bolivia, including a report-back to the OAS Permanent Council, and collaborate through the OAS in close regional coordination on next steps. Deputy Secretary Landau reaffirmed the United States’ commitment to supporting U.S. companies as trusted, long-term partners in Brunei’s economic development. The principals committed to follow-up consultations to advance the initiatives identified during this inaugural Strategic Dialogue and agreed to convene again in 2027. title: Under Secretary Rogers Hosts Digital NEXT Delegation with FTC Chairman Ferguson and Elon Musk and Announces New Tech Industry Partnership to Advance Digital Freedom
text: Home Office of the Spokesperson Press Releases … Under Secretary Rogers Hosts Digital NEXT Delegation with FTC Chairman Ferguson and Elon Musk and Announces New Tech Industry Partnership to Advance Digital Freedom hide Under Secretary Rogers Hosts Digital NEXT Delegation with FTC Chairman Ferguson and Elon Musk and Announces New Tech Industry Partnership to Advance Digital Freedom Media Note Office of the Spokesperson July 31, 2026 Last week, Under Secretary of State for Public Diplomacy Sarah Rogers convened 47 foreign technology policymakers and government representatives from 30 countries in San Francisco, California, for Digital NEXT: Protecting Digital Liberties in the AI Era. The delegation engaged in tailored dialogues with leading American technology companies to observe how the U.S. private sector is proactively addressing digital freedom challenges and offering compelling alternatives to burdensome regulatory models that infringe on privacy and freedom of expression. During a capstone fireside chat hosted by the Silicon Valley Office of Protocol that included conversations with Elon Musk, Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew N. Ferguson, and Tim Hwang of the Foundation for American Innovation, Under Secretary Rogers underscored the importance of protecting children online in ways that do not unduly restrict freedom of speech or stifle innovation. Under Secretary Rogers also launched the Freedom Tech Excellence Program (FTEP), a new partnership between the Department and leading technology companies, civil society organizations, and think tanks to advance U.S. digital freedom objectives globally. Through FTEP, private sector organizations will send experts for limited-term assignments to infuse their expertise into the Department’s digital freedom work on critical issues including promoting online freedom of expression, privacy-enhancing technologies, responsible AI governance, and countering digital surveillance. FTEP gives participating organizations direct insight into how these policies impact their organizational interests and operations while helping the Department stay ahead of challenges that affect both American businesses and the rights of Americans online. Under Secretary Rogers is pleased to announce FTEP’s inaugural partners: Palantir Technologies, Anduril Industries, Bitcoin Policy Institute, and Victims of Communism Foundation, and looks forward to welcoming additional organizations into the partnership. For further information, please contact Partnerships@state.gov . Tags Freedom of Speech and Expression Office of the Spokesperson Under Secretary for Public Diplomacy

title: United States Sanctioning Iran’s Mahan Air Network and IRGC-Linked Front Company
text: Home Office of the Spokesperson Press Releases … United States Sanctioning Iran’s Mahan Air Network and IRGC-Linked Front Company hide United States Sanctioning Iran’s Mahan Air Network and IRGC-Linked Front Company Press Statement Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesperson July 30, 2026 The United States today sanctioned six entities and individuals in China, India, Russia, and Iran that enable the Iranian regime’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). These include entities that support Mahan Air, the IRGC’s airline of choice for moving weapons, military personnel, and equipment. Today’s action also targets DadeNegar Startup Studio, an IRGC-affiliated front company supporting Iranian military targeting by soliciting locations of American and Israeli equipment in the Middle East. The United States calls on the international community, particularly companies and individuals doing business with Mahan Air or any other sanctioned Iranian carrier, to recognize the serious risks raised by continuing such engagement. The United States will continue to expose and disrupt entities providing the IRGC with the tools and information it uses to threaten American personnel, our partners, and regional stability. OFAC is taking this action pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13224, as amended, which targets terrorist groups, their supporters, and those who aid acts of terrorism, and in furtherance of the President’s National Security Presidential Memorandum 2 (NSPM-2), which directs the U.S. government to deny the IRGC access to assets and resources that sustain its destabilizing activities. On October 12, 2011, OFAC designated Mahan Air pursuant to E.O. 13224 for providing financial, material, and technological support to Iran’s IRGC-Qods Force (IRGC-QF), which OFAC designated pursuant to E.O. 13224 in October 2007 for providing material support to multiple terrorist organizations. The U.S. Department of State designated the IRGC itself pursuant to the counterproliferation authority E.O. 13382 in 2007, and OFAC designated the IRGC pursuant to E.O. 13224 in October 2017 for providing support to the IRGC-QF. F or more information on today’s action, please see Treasury’s press release . title: U.S. Department of State and U.S. Department of Health and Human Services on Strengthening Vaccine Safety, Accountability, and American Leadership in Global Health
text: Home Office of the Spokesperson Press Releases … U.S. Department of State and U.S. Department of Health and Human Services on Strengthening Vaccine Safety, Accountability, and American Leadership in Global Health hide U.S. Department of State and U.S. Department of Health and Human Services on Strengthening Vaccine Safety, Accountability, and American Leadership in Global Health Media Note Office of the Spokesperson July 29, 2026 The United States is committed to advancing global health in a manner that reflects American interests, scientific integrity, and accountability to the American people. Under President Trump’s leadership, the United States has made clear that American taxpayer dollars must support transparent, evidence-based programs that deliver measurable health outcomes. Last year, President Trump directed Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. and Secretary of State Marco Rubio to engage directly with Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance (Gavi), and secure meaningful reforms before the United States would consider future support. Those discussions resulted in significant commitments that strengthen vaccine safety, improve public health, and better align Gavi’s work with the principles of Gold Standard Science and transparency. Based on those commitments, the United States will immediately release all $600 million in Congressionally appropriated funds to Gavi for both FY25 and FY26. Gavi has committed to work towards transitioning mercury-containing vaccines and expanding access to newer, mercury-free alternatives. Specifically, in partnership with Gavi’s Board and countries, Gavi will make every effort to: transition mercury-containing meningococcal A vaccines with mercury-free vaccines that protect against additional meningococcal strains; transition mercury-containing pentavalent DTP-Hib-HepB vaccines to mercury-free hexavalent vaccines that also protect against polio; transition mercury-containing pneumococcal vaccines to mercury-free vaccines that protect against additional pneumococcal strains; and transition mercury-containing hepatitis B vaccines to mercury-free alternatives. The Administration believes reducing reliance on mercury-containing vaccines, where suitable alternatives are available, is a pro-vaccine, pro-innovation policy. The United States and the European Union removed mercury from most childhood vaccines 25 years ago. As of June 2025, CDC’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices no longer recommends any mercury-containing vaccines. Children in Africa, Asia, and Latin America deserve access to the same higher-quality, mercury-free vaccines, and these changes will also expand protection against additional disease strains. Achieving these transitions will require manufacturers to expand production capacity, countries to adopt newer vaccine formulations, and Gavi’s governing Board to complete the necessary approvals. The United States recognizes these implementation challenges but welcomes Gavi’s commitment to work toward these goals through transparent governance and responsible stewardship. Gavi has already implemented additional reforms requested by the United States including: Ending the promotion and procurement of COVID-19 vaccines for routine immunization programs; and Finalizing extensive operational reforms including the reorganization and downsizing of staff in Geneva and instituting a partnership accountability framework that decreases funding for and reforms Gavi’s engagement with other partners, including the World Health Organization (WHO). Gavi has further committed to establishing an integrated and dedicated Secretariat function to monitor and review developments in vaccine science, including vaccine safety. In addition, given the sizeable contribution the United States is making to improve access to vaccines, the United States expects to resume its place on the Gavi Board. In this role, the United States will continue to hold Gavi accountable for measurable progress toward these commitments. It will evaluate any future U.S. support based on demonstrated performance, accountability, and implementation of these reforms. The United States also reaffirms that it will not provide U.S. Government funding to the World Health Organization through Gavi. President Trump has made clear that American leadership in global health must be rooted in accountability, scientific excellence, and measurable results. The Department of Health and Human Services and the Department of State will continue to ensure that U.S. global health programs and partnerships uphold Gold Standard Science, rigorous independent review, transparency, responsible stewardship of taxpayer resources, and better health outcomes around the world. title: Countering Iran’s Exploitation of the Strait of Hormuz
text: Home Office of the Spokesperson Press Releases … Countering Iran’s Exploitation of the Strait of Hormuz hide Countering Iran’s Exploitation of the Strait of Hormuz Press Statement Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesperson July 29, 2026 Today, the United States designated the Persian Gulf Marine Insurance Company and Hormuz Safe Marine Services Authority, two Iranian entities backed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), for running coercive “insurance” schemes that extort international shipping transiting the Strait of Hormuz. These entities manufacture risk—including the threat of vessel seizures—and then charge commercial vessels for coverage against dangers created by the regime itself, generating revenue that sustains IRGC operations and Iran’s broader campaign of regional destabilization. The United States also designated eight companies operating vessels that have transported illicit Iranian crude oil and petrochemical products to China and the United Arab Emirates. These vessels form part of Iran’s “shadow fleet,” which the regime relies on to evade sanctions. Today’s designations support the U.S. Navy’s enforcement of a blockade on Iranian ports and coastline and add to a sustained campaign that has now sanctioned more than 100 vessels this year. The United States will continue to hold Iran accountable for weaponizing vital international waterways and evading sanctions through shadow fleet operations and deceptive financial schemes. Protecting navigational rights and freedoms in the Strait of Hormuz is a global interest, and the United States will act, alongside partners, to ensure Iran cannot hold international commerce hostage to finance its malign activities. We will continue working with allies to isolate the regime diplomatically and economically until it ceases its destabilizing behavior. Today’s action was taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets Iran’s financial, petroleum, and petrochemical sectors. It continues the robust sanctions campaign targeting Iranian oil sales in support of the President’s National Security Presidential Memorandum 2 (NSPM-2). For more information on today’s action, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press release . title: Opportunities for Growth in U.S.-Peru Relations
text: Home Office of the Spokesperson Press Releases … Opportunities for Growth in U.S.-Peru Relations hide Opportunities for Growth in U.S.-Peru Relations Fact Sheet Office of the Spokesperson July 29, 2026 The Presidential Delegation to the July 28 inauguration of President Fujimori, led by Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau, signals U.S. commitment to Peru and highlights the strength of our partnership. The strong ties between the United States and Peru are underpinned by an enduring friendship spanning 200 years of diplomatic relations. The Trump Administration looks forward to working with President Fujimori to bring security and prosperity to the United States, Peru, and to our hemisphere. Enhancing Security: The United States applauds President Fujimori’s focus on fighting transnational criminal organizations that threaten American and Peruvian security and prosperity and to improve citizen security across Peru. Peru is a valuable member of the Americans Counter-Cartel Coalition (A3C), and the Department of War intends to scale up counter-narcotics cooperation with Peru, particularly in the northern tri-border region. The Department of State’s Bureau of Counterterrorism will send a Department of Justice team to Peru to improve bilateral coordination and information sharing on efforts to combat the Tren de Aragua, which President Trump designated as a Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO) . The Bureau of Counterterrorism will also help disrupt FTO operations by supporting President Fujimori’s border security efforts through the expansion of biometrics collection in prisons and border regions and the donation of two Explosive Trace Detection machines to Jorge Chavez International Airport. The Department of Commerce will convene U.S. industry partners in Lima in September to discuss opportunities for U.S. technology providers under President Fujimori’s plans to construct nine new prisons . The Department of State’s Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL) has a long and successful history of working with Peru tocombat narco-trafficking, illegal mining, and other illicit activities. With newly created and expanded vetted units , we can effectively support President Fujimori’s efforts to dismantle organized crime groups. The newly created, INL-funded Peruvian National Police (PNP) Complex Crime Investigative Unit vetted unit, managed by FBI, will carry out complex organized crime investigations. Following two years of successful operations against transnational criminal organizations, we expanded the PNP Transnational Criminal Investigative Unit, run by DHS and supported by State . INL will provide additional specialized training and equipment to help Peru combat illegal mining and associated criminal activities. Increasing Trade and Investment: Peru’s stable economy has attracted U.S. investment across multiple sectors, and President Fujimori’s pro-business plans will create opportunities for the U.S. private sector and strengthen Peru’s economic growth. Ambassador Navarro will lead a “Peru is Open for Business” trade mission to the United States this year. In addition, the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) is actively seeking investment opportunities in energy, infrastructure, critical minerals, and other priority sectors and will send a business development mission to Peru this year. To increase our collaboration in emerging technology, the United States will host an AI Summit on September 8 in Lima. The Department of War will provide a cyber-advisor to work side by side with the Fujimori government on cyber security issues. To identify new areas for cooperation in mining, the United States and Peru will establish a critical minerals working group to implement the Critical Minerals MOU signed in February. An up to $5 million DFC investment in Peru’s mining sector will support the establishment of the reprocessing plant, which will enhance processing technologies and refining capacity in Peru, strengthening the supply chain for critical minerals. To improve Peru’s port infrastructure, the United States will continue to support the expansion of the Port of Callao – Peru’s most consequential port – through the work of the Army Corps of Engineers. We will also work with the Fujimori administration to identify opportunities for U.S. industry to invest in the port’s growth and future success. Space Cooperation: The United States will expand on decades of successful cooperation to advance science, education, and development of the global space industry. Peru has taken a leadership role in the Artemis Accords. We look forward to expanding civil, commercial, and defense related space cooperation that enhance American and Peruvian prosperity and security, including: Developing, together with Peru, a space consortium – a public-private effort focused on education, military, civilian, and commercial opportunities – to grow Peru’s space economy. Sending a Peruvian liaison officer to work directly with U.S. Space Command. Assisting Peru in finalizing their 10-year space strategy. Donating a high-powered telescope by the end of 2026. Providing additional scholarships for education in space-related disciplines such as engineering, aerospace, astrophysics, cyber-security, and related fields. Disaster Preparedness and Relief: The United States stands ready to help Peru strengthen its preparedness to respond to El Niño weather events. We applaud President Fujimori for developing a comprehensive response plan. FEMA will lead a series of virtual workshops for Peru on disaster risk management. The USNS Comfort Hospital Ship will visit Peru in early 2027, augmenting Peru’s capacity to provide medical support. The United States has pre-positioned emergency blankets and hygiene kits for emergency assistance for quick response. The Department of War will donate mobile bridges to assist with potential floods and continue to upgrade several of the 18 regional emergency communication centers originally built under the Humanitarian Assistance Program. title: U.S. Department of State Debars 14 Persons for Violating or Conspiring to Violate the Arms Export Control Act
text: Home Bureau of Political-Military Affairs Remarks & Releases … U.S. Department of State Debars 14 Persons for Violating or Conspiring to Violate the Arms Export Control Act hide U.S. Department of State Debars 14 Persons for Violating or Conspiring to Violate the Arms Export Control Act Other Release Bureau of Political-Military Affairs July 24, 2026 On July 24, 2026, the U.S. Department of State published in the Federal Register a notice of 14 persons statutorily debarred for having been convicted of violating, or conspiring to violate, the Arms Export Control Act (22 U.S.C. 2751, et seq. ). This action, pursuant to section 127.7(b) of the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) (22 CFR parts 120-130), highlights the Department’s responsibility to protect the integrity of U.S. defense trade. This notice is provided for purposes of making the public aware that these statutorily debarred persons are prohibited from participating directly or indirectly in activities regulated by the ITAR. This includes any brokering activities and any export from or temporary import into the United States of defense articles, related technical data, or defense services regulated by the ITAR. The Department’s Office of Defense Trade Controls Compliance in the Bureau of Political-Military Affairs, working in collaboration with the Department of Justice, Homeland Security Investigations, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation, identified the persons subject to statutory debarment based on their criminal conviction by a court of the United States. Under the terms of the statutory debarment, these persons are prohibited from participating directly or indirectly in any activities that are subject to the ITAR. Each person on this list will remain debarred until the Department approves an application request for reinstatement. All persons engaged in activities subject to the ITAR should be vigilant in their compliance with all export control regulations and ensure that their activities do not involve debarred persons. The notice of statutory debarment listing the names of the debarred individuals was published in the Federal Register on July 24. A full list of all persons subject to statutory debarment is available on the website of the PM Bureau’s Directorate of Defense Trade Controls (DDTC) at: Statutory Debarment List . For additional information, please contact the Office of the Under Secretary for Arms Control and International Security at T_Outreach_PM@state.gov . title: Advancing American Safety, Strength, and Prosperity in Southeast Asia
text: Home Office of the Spokesperson Press Releases … Advancing American Safety, Strength, and Prosperity in Southeast Asia hide Advancing American Safety, Strength, and Prosperity in Southeast Asia Fact Sheet Office of the Spokesperson July 22, 2026 Secretary of State Marco Rubio is on travel to Manila, Philippines, July 21-23, to engage with ASEAN and regional leaders to advance the United States’ vision for a Free and Open Indo-Pacific, reaffirm U.S. commitment to ASEAN centrality, and strengthen the U.S.-Philippine alliance. The U.S.-ASEAN Comprehensive Strategic Partnership has helped Southeast Asia to grow and prosper while creating opportunities for Americans and American businesses. Recognizing the strategic importance of Southeast Asia to the future of American security and prosperity, the United States is investing over $2.5 billion to strengthen security cooperation, build strategic infrastructure, advance technology-related cooperation, bolster energy security, and combat transnational crime in Southeast Asia. Advancing Technology of the Future in Southeast Asia U.S.-ASEAN AI SPARK: Working with Congress, the United States will make Southeast Asia a focus for American AI exports, which will accelerate the region’s digital transformation and economic growth. To achieve this, the United States is launching a new Pax Silica initiative, AI SPARK, which will support American AI exports in the region by providing financial and technical support to Southeast Asian governments interested in deploying the U.S. AI stack for public-sector applications. Philippines Trusted Technology Roadmap: The United States, working with Congress, plans to provide $10 million to substantially strengthen how the Philippines’ critical information and communications technology (ICT) infrastructure is secured and modernized. Bolstering Energy Security in Southeast Asia Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) Threshold Program: The MCC Board approved a $60 million Threshold Program grant to the Philippines to enable energy sector investment, strengthen energy institutions, and expand opportunities for American commercial engagement. Securing Critical Minerals Supply Chains in the Mekong: In support of the Mekong-U.S. Partnership, the United States, working with Congress, is securing critical mineral supply chains through $17 million in funding toward the Mekong Minerals Partnership. Advancing Energy Infrastructure and Energy Security: Through the Japan-U.S.-Mekong Power Partnership (JUMPP), the United States, working with Congress, intends to provide $5 million to develop regional power markets, promote LNG market development, deploy U.S. grid technologies, and strengthen capacity for reliable energy infrastructure and cross-border electricity trade across Cambodia, Laos, Thailand, and Vietnam. Philippines Critical Minerals Support: The United States, working with Congress, plans to provide $4 million to drive mining projects toward investment and offtake and to help identify investment-scale opportunities. Investing Strategically in Southeast Asian Infrastructure Developing Energy Infrastructure in the Indo-Pacific: The United States is investing $1.5 billion to establish an investment platform to facilitate the buildout of energy security infrastructure across the Indo-Pacific. This deal represents the single largest project investment in the International Development Finance Corporation’s (DFC) history. Strategic Infrastructure Investments: The United States announced plans to work with Congress to provide over $100 million in strategic assistance for infrastructure and other investments in the Philippines, focused on Subic Bay in the Luzon Economic Corridor. The Department will fund upgrades including port facilities and a fuel storage terminal with 120+ million liters of capacity. Combating Crime and Enhancing Law Enforcement Cooperation Combating Transnational Crime: The United States plans to provide $2.5 million to unite ASEAN countries through tailored interventions against scams, cybercrime, drug trafficking, and money laundering. Philippines Coast Guard Pier: The United States is providing $9 million to expand a Philippine Coast Guard Pier in Palawan to enhance Philippine maritime law enforcement presence and sustain operations in the South China Sea. Delivering U.S. Commercial Deals Philippine Airlines and Boeing: The United States welcomes the recent announcement by Philippine Airlines of its intent to purchase up to 20 Boeing 787 aircraft powered by GE Aerospace GEnx engines. This significant announcement speaks to the deepening commercial ties between the United States and the Philippines. Commercial Diplomacy: U.S. companies operating in the ASEAN region generated over $14 billion in commercial deals over the past year, supporting the potential creation of more than 40,000 American jobs in sectors including energy, aerospace, health, technology, and transportation. Strengthening Security Cooperation in Southeast Asia Expansion of Foreign Military Financing: The United States will allocate $100 million in military grant assistance to the Philippines for fiscal year 2026, a $60 million increase over historical annual funding levels, to enhance the Philippines’ ability to defend its sovereignty and deter conflict. Increasing International Military Education and Training (IMET): The United States is providing $21.45 million to enhance military education and training for ASEAN countries. The United States will launch a new IMET program in Brunei and restart the IMET program in Cambodia. Advancing Counterterrorism: The United States plans to provide $19 million this year to support investigations, prosecution, information sharing, and training and equipment for Philippine counterterrorism efforts which advances the security of the American Homeland. Strategic AI and Cyber for National Security: The United States is funding a $6.5 million contract providing the Philippines access to the Rhombus AI Concierge platform, which will enable data-driven AI analytics and real-time predictive analysis to inform strategic national security decisions. The United States is also providing $3 million for cyber-related training to the Philippines. Safely Demining the Region: The United States is providing over $130 million to continue demining and clearance of unexploded ordnance (UXO) in Cambodia, Laos, and Vietnam as part of the United States’ commitment to war legacy efforts. Improving Global Health Security U.S.-Philippines Health Strategic Objective Agreement: The U.S. Government and the Government of the Philippines signed a five-year Strategic Objective Agreement. The agreement contains a jointly funded plan for up to $685 million to improve and sustain capacity to detect, treat, and prevent HIV and tuberculosis, and strengthen global health security. title: New Visa Restriction Policy to Deter and Dismantle Cyberscams and Sextortion
text: Home Office of the Spokesperson Press Releases … New Visa Restriction Policy to Deter and Dismantle Cyberscams and Sextortion hide New Visa Restriction Policy to Deter and Dismantle Cyberscams and Sextortion Press Statement Marco Rubio, Secretary of State July 23, 2026 As President Trump made clear in E.O. 14390 on Combatting Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens, his administration is taking action to counter an unprecedented threat from online investment scams. Often orchestrated by Chinese transnational criminal organizations, scammers have defrauded U.S. citizens of at least $10 billion in 2024 alone while fueling corruption, money laundering, and human trafficking. American children also have been specifically targeted by offenders operating overseas for sextortion scams, devastating families and futures. Today, I am announcing a new global visa restriction policy under Section 212(a)(3)(C) of the Immigration and Nationality Act. This policy targets individuals responsible for, or complicit in, cybercrime and cyber-enabled crime, such as those involved in cyberscams, and sextortion. Immediate family members of individuals engaged in such illicit activities may also be subjected to visa restrictions. The Trump Administration is deploying every tool at our disposal—sanctions, prosecutions, asset seizures, extradition requests, and international law enforcement cooperation—to dismantle criminal scam networks and impose costs on those who enable them. By restricting visa issuance to those who are responsible for or complicit in these criminal enterprises, we are sending a clear message: The United States will go after those who prey on our citizens.
